article_content: E! True Hollywood Story, the long-running documentary series known for exploring the lives of celebrities and public figures, is turning its lens on Casey Anthony — the woman whose 2011 trial captivated the nation. Acquitted of murdering her two-year-old daughter, Caylee, in July 2011 after a six-week trial in Orlando, Anthony became a lightning rod for media frenzy. Time magazine dubbed it 'the social media trial of the century,' and now, nearly a decade later, E! is airing a one-hour special featuring interviews with journalists, former friends, defense attorneys, and even Zenaida Fernandez Gonzalez — the real woman whose name was falsely used by Anthony to explain her daughter’s disappearance. Caylee vanished in June 2008 and was found dead in nearby woods half a year later. While Anthony was cleared of murder and manslaughter charges, she was convicted of lying to police — a detail often overshadowed by the emotional weight of the case. The documentary also highlights the devastating impact on Zenaida Fernandez Gonzalez, an innocent woman subjected to online threats, hate campaigns, and even death threats because of the false narrative. She has since filed a defamation lawsuit against Anthony, who appeared in court disguised in a wig and sunglasses to give testimony. Since her acquittal, Anthony has remained out of the public eye, burdened by over $217,000 in legal fees and the unresolved civil suit. Meanwhile, her defense attorney, Jose Baez, faces two formal complaints from the Florida Bar — one for allegedly withholding evidence during pre-trial discovery, and another for failing to disclose that Anthony was already serving probation for check fraud while jailed before her murder trial. The E! special, airing tonight at 10 p.m. ET, blends courtroom footage, dramatic reenactments, and firsthand accounts — continuing the network’s tradition of blending journalism with tabloid-style storytelling.

Hon blev friad från mord på sin tvåårige dotter, Caylee, i juli 2011 efter en sex veckor lång rättegång i Orlando, och blev en blixtråd för media. Time-magasin döpte den till 'sociala mediers rättegång av århundradet', och nu, nästan tio år senare, sänder E! en en timme lång speciel med intervjuer med journalister, tidigare vänner, försvarsadvokater och även Zenaida Fernandez Gonzalez – den verkliga kvinnan vars namn användes falskt av Anthony för att förklara dotterns försvinnande. Caylee försvann i juni 2008 och hittades död i skogen halvår senare. Även om Anthony frikändes från mord och manslakt, blev hon dömd för att ha gett felaktig information till polisen – ett detalj som ofta övergås av det emotionella trycket i fallet. Dokumentären lyfter också fram den förödande effekten på Zenaida Fernandez Gonzalez, en oskyldig kvinna som utsattes för hot på internet, hatkampanjer och till och med dödshot på grund av den falska berättelsen. Hon har sedan lämnat in en skadeståndsklagomål mot Anthony, som dök upp i rätten klädd i peruk, basebollkappa och solglasögon för att ge sitt vittnesmål. Efter frikännandet har Anthony hållit sig utanför det offentliga fältet, belastad med mer än 217 000 dollar i rättskostnader och den olösta civilrättsliga processen. Samtidigt står hennes försvarsadvokat, Jose Baez, inför två formella anmälningar från Florida Bar – en för att ha underlåtit att lämna över bevis under förhandsutredningen, och en annan för att inte ha meddelat domstolen att Anthony redan tjänade en år lång beväringsstraff för kontrollfusk medan hon var i fängelse innan mordrättegången började. Den speciella E! dokumentären, som sänds ikväll klockan 22:00 ET, kombinerar rättegångsinspelningar, dramatiska återuppvisningar och personliga berättelser – och fortsätter nätverkets tradition av att blanda journalistik med tabloid-stil.

article_content: Manchester United defender Patrice Evra is on the verge of a permanent move to Italian club Juventus. The Frenchman is prepared to sign a two-year contract worth approximately £55,000 per week, with Juventus having made a formal £2 million offer to United. The deal could be finalized within 48 hours after Evra requested the club to respect his decision to leave Old Trafford. His primary motivation is believed to be family-related, with his wife, Sandra, eager to relocate abroad. Evra’s playing opportunities at United have been reduced following the signing of Luke Shaw from Southampton. Reports in June indicated that Shaw, a £28 million acquisition, was assured he would become the first-choice left-back under new manager Louis van Gaal. With no European football this season, United will play fewer matches weekly, further limiting Evra’s chances to feature. Although his contract was extended by one year at the end of last season, it now appears highly likely that Evra will begin next season in Juventus’ black-and-white stripes, reuniting with fellow French international and former United midfielder Paul Pogba. United officials valued Evra’s leadership and experience, particularly during David Moyes’ turbulent tenure, when his professionalism stood out amid the club’s pursuit of Leighton Baines. His departure will be met with regret by many at Old Trafford. Evra spent eight successful years at United, winning five Premier League titles and reaching three UEFA Champions League finals — including the 2008 penalty-shootout victory over Chelsea in Moscow. His exit follows a wave of departures from United’s veteran core: Ryan Giggs retired, while Rio Ferdinand and Nemanja Vidic left upon contract expiry. Giggs remains at the club as an assistant coach, but the loss of on-field experience is significant — the four players combined for 2,097 United appearances and 80 medals. Meanwhile, United continue to monitor Juventus midfielder Arturo Vidal, who represented Chile at the 2014 World Cup. However, Juventus are demanding £37 million for the Chilean, a figure well beyond United’s current valuation. While initial inquiries have been made, a deal remains distant.

article_content: A 13-year-old girl from Florida, Yaquelin Galvez Don, and her 15-year-old boyfriend, Pedro Solis, are facing adult charges after allegedly plotting for over a week to kill her mother, Luz Galvez. The plan, carried out on March 9 in their Ocala garage, stemmed from the mother’s opposition to their relationship, which they discussed extensively via Facebook. During the attack, Solis slashed Galvez’s throat. Miraculously, she survived after Solis changed his mind and rushed her to the hospital—dropping her on the curb before driving away. Galvez, who underwent emergency surgery, identified both teens as her attackers the same day. Her husband, Jorge Don-Brianes, who uses a wheelchair, was also threatened during the incident but unable to intervene. Both teens have been denied bail and are being held without bond. Solis’s mother, Maria Hernandez, says she repeatedly warned him against the relationship, calling him a kind boy who was deeply attached to Yaquelin. Meanwhile, authorities say the teens’ motive was retaliation for parental interference. Yaquelin’s attorney expressed disappointment that the court decided to try her as an adult, noting that juveniles require different evaluations. If convicted, both face life in prison.

Planen genomfördes den 9 mars i deras garage i Ocala och var ett svar på moderns motstånd mot deras relation, som de diskuterade omfattande via Facebook. Under attacken skar Solis Galvez hals. Hon överlevde, i en oväntad vändning, när Solis ändrade sig och körde henne till sjukhuset – där han släppte henne på trottoarkanten innan han körde iväg. Båda tonåringarna har nekats borgen och hålls utan borg. Myndigheterna säger att tonåringarnas motiv var hämnd för föräldrars ingripande. article_content: In a bold and widely criticized proposal, Vladimir Zhirinovsky, leader of Russia’s Liberal Democratic Party and deputy speaker of the State Duma, has suggested extending public health regulations beyond smoking to include sex and food consumption. With Russia preparing to enforce a nationwide ban on smoking in public areas, Zhirinovsky argues the measures don’t go far enough. He claims that Russians live significantly shorter lives than people in Western countries due to overeating, excessive smoking, and too much sexual activity. To curb this, he proposed a system where citizens would receive government-issued vouchers allowing sexual intercourse only once every three months. He also recommended banning smoking entirely except in fully enclosed private spaces—such as a car with all windows shut or an empty home—where individuals could, in his words, 'shut all the windows and get yourself poisoned.' Zhirinovsky framed these ideas as necessary interventions to reverse what he sees as a national decline in life expectancy, asking, 'Why should we perish?' when others abroad live longer.

Medan Ryssland förbereder sig för att införa ett nationellt förbud mot rökning i offentliga platser, hävdar Zhirinovskij att dessa åtgärder inte går långt nog. Han påstår att ryssar lever betydligt kortare liv än människor i västliga länder på grund av överätande, överdriven rökning och för mycket könsliv. För att minska detta föreslår han ett system där medborgare får utgåvor från staten som tillåter sexuell aktivitet endast en gång per tre månader. Han rekommenderade också att förbjuda rökning helt utom i fullständigt avslutade privata rum — såsom en bil med alla fönster stängda eller ett tomt hem — där individer, i hans ord, 'kan stänga alla fönster och förgifta dig själv.' Zhirinovskij presenterade dessa idéer som nödvändiga ingripanden för att vända det han ser som en nationell minskning av livslängden, och frågar: 'Varför ska vi dö?' när andra i utlandet lever längre.

article_content: NASA has confirmed that the 6-ton Upper Atmospheric Research Satellite (UARS), launched in 1991, will re-enter Earth’s atmosphere on Friday, September 23, 2011, and will not pass over North America during that time. As a result, residents of the United States will not witness the spectacular sight of the satellite breaking apart in the sky. Though most of the satellite will burn up due to atmospheric friction, approximately 1,200 pounds of metal debris is expected to reach the Earth’s surface. These fragments could scatter across a wide area between 57 degrees north and 57 degrees south latitude — regions home to billions of people. Astrophotographer Thierry Legault, based in Dunkerque, France, captured rare video footage of UARS tumbling through space eight days before re-entry. Using his Celestron EdgeHD 14-inch telescope, he observed rapid fluctuations in brightness, likely due to the satellite spinning after a past collision with space debris. NASA stresses that the risk to public safety is extremely low. Since the dawn of the Space Age in the 1950s, no confirmed injuries from falling space debris have ever been recorded. The satellite is far smaller than past re-entering objects like the 135-ton Russian Mir space station or the 100-ton Skylab. Re-entry timing and location remain uncertain due to unpredictable atmospheric density, which affects drag. Even a minor timing error could shift the impact zone by hundreds of miles. The Joint Space Operations Center at Vandenberg Air Force Base continues tracking UARS. Most debris is expected to land in oceans, which cover two-thirds of the planet. Still, NASA urges anyone who believes they’ve found a piece of UARS not to touch it and to contact local authorities instead. UARS was designed to study ozone, winds, and temperatures in the stratosphere. Today, NASA designs satellites to either fully disintegrate on re-entry or boost themselves into graveyard orbits — a response to the growing threat of space junk, which now numbers over 370,000 tracked objects, largely due to events like China’s 2007 anti-satellite test and the 2009 satellite collision.

Som ett resultat kommer invånare i USA inte att kunna bevittna det spektakulära synet av satelliten som bryts sönder i himlen. Även om de flesta delarna av satelliten kommer att brinna upp på grund av luftmotstånd, förväntas cirka 544 kilogram metallskrot nå jordens yta. Dessa fragment kan spridas över ett stort område mellan 57 grader norr och 57 grader syd — regioner där miljarder människor bor. Astrofotografen Thierry Legault, baserad i Dunkerque, Frankrike, tog sällsynta videoklipp av UARS som snurrar genom rymden åtta dagar före återinträdet. Med hjälp av sin Celestron EdgeHD 14-tums teleskop observerade han snabba variationer i ljusstyrka, troligen på grund av att satelliten snurrar efter en tidigare kollision med rymdsopor. NASA betonar att risken för allmänheten är extremt liten. Sedan rymdålderns början på 1950-talet har inga bekräftade skador eller personskador orsakade av fallande rymdobjekt registrerats. Satelliten är mycket mindre än tidigare återinträdande objekt som den 135-tonners ryska Mir-rymdstationen eller de 100-tonners Skylab. Tiden och platsen för återinträdet är fortfarande osäker på grund av den förutsägbara lufttätheten, vilket påverkar luftmotståndet. Även en liten felaktig tidsskattning kan förflytta nedslagszonen med hundratals mil. Joint Space Operations Center vid Vandenberg Air Force Base fortsätter att spåra UARS. De flesta resterna förväntas hamna i haven, som täcker två tredjedelar av planeten. Trots detta uppmanar NASA alla som tror att de hittat en del av UARS att inte röra vid den, utan att kontakta lokala myndigheter istället. UARS togs upp för att studera ozon, vindar och temperaturer i stratosfären. Idag designar NASA satelliter så att de antingen helt brinner upp vid återinträde eller får bränsle för att flyga upp till högre, långvariga banor — ett svar på det växande hotet från rymdsopor, som numera uppgår till över 370 000 spårbara objekt, främst på grund av händelser som Kinas anti-satellittest 2007 och kollisionen 2009 mellan två satelliter.

article_content: Honasa Consumer, the parent company behind the popular toxin-free beauty brand Mamaearth, saw its shares jump nearly 20% on Thursday, hitting a new high of Rs 422.50 on the BSE. This surge followed the release of stellar Q2 financial results, including a 94% year-over-year spike in net profit. Revenue climbed 21% YoY to Rs 496 crore, while EBITDA margins expanded to a record 8.1%, up 170 basis points from last year. The company attributes this momentum to strong sales volume and smarter ad spending. In the first half of FY24, overall revenue grew 33% YoY—nearly four times the average growth of India’s FMCG sector—and net profit soared an astonishing 1,377% to Rs 54 crore. Mamaearth, now among India’s top 15 beauty brands, continues to outpace legacy players. Other brands under Honasa are also accelerating: The Derma Co now generates Rs 380 crore annually, Aqualogica hits Rs 180 crore, and Dr. Sheth, acquired just a few years ago, has grown 30-fold to surpass Rs 150 crore in annual revenue. BBlunt’s product business has tripled since acquisition. Management notes that Q2’s numbers were inflated slightly because some revenue was moved from Q1 due to an ERP system rollout in June 2023, making the first-half figures a truer reflection of underlying strength. Despite a rocky post-IPO journey—listing at Rs 330 after an IPO price of Rs 324, then falling to Rs 256 before rebounding—the stock regained momentum after Jefferies analyst Vivek Maheshwari upgraded it to a 'high-conviction buy' and raised the target price to Rs 530. Investors are now betting on sustained margin expansion and continued brand-led growth through FY26.

article_content: By Martha De Lacey. PUBLISHED: 09:38 EST, 22 May 2013. | UPDATED: 09:38 EST, 22 May 2013. I owe Dr. Deepa Apte — the gentle, softly spoken medic-turned-Ayurvedic masseuse who slathered my entire body in fragrant sesame oil for an hour — a sincere apology. Two-thirds of the way through my decadent session on her massage table, my consciousness slipped into the most delicious state of sleep — and, as body parts are prone to do when drifting off, my leg involuntarily spasmed, kicking the good doctor in the face. It’s a testament to the power of her soothing hands and flawless technique that I managed to leave all of life’s stresses at the door of her North Greenwich day spa and drift so completely into peace. Ayurveda Pura, an award-winning wellness center, practices Ayurveda — a 5,000-year-old Indian holistic medical system whose name means 'science of life.' It seeks physical and mental harmony with nature through diet, yoga, massage, detoxification, herbal remedies, meditation, and daily lifestyle practices. In other words: massages are essential. This is my kind of belief system. As Dr. Deepa explained in her softly scented room, Ayurveda views all things in the universe — including humans — as composed of five basic elements: space, air, fire, water, and earth. Illness, according to Ayurveda, arises from an imbalance within these elements in a person’s constitution. Treatment aims to restore harmony and reinstate health. These elements combine into three doshas: Vata (air + space), Pitta (fire + water), and Kapha (water + earth). While everyone possesses all three, the dominant combination defines an individual’s unique Prakriti, or constitutional type. After holding my wrist and assessing my body type — Vata-Pitta: ambitious, hardworking, hungry, medium build, often with a gap between teeth (all eerily accurate) — Dr. Deepa laid me on her soft table. Unlike deep tissue, Swedish, or sports massages — which focus on pressure, joint cracking, or forced movement — an Ayurvedic massage is a gentle, flowing, deeply sensory experience. Instead of pounding knots, she slathered my skin in edible, herb-infused oils (in Ayurveda, nothing is applied to the body that isn’t safe to eat) and glided her palms over me, her touch never breaking contact. Combined with the soft, plinky-plunky music, the warm dim room, and the cushioned bed, her presence sent me drifting into sleep. Hence the kick. When the hour ended, Dr. Deepa gently woke me, allowed me to rinse off the oil (she’d used enough to deep-fry a person whole), and poured me a fresh herbal tea while I showered — to rehydrate and prolong the blissful calm. As I floated back out into Greenwich, the world seemed muted, less frantic, and far less urgent. To-do list? What to-do list? Ayurveda Pura Health Spa & Beauty Centre, London, SE10 0BA. www.ayurvedapura.com | 020 8312 8383
translated_content: Av Martha De Lacey. PUBLICERAD: 09:38 EST, 22 maj 2013. | UPPDATERAD: 09:38 EST, 22 maj 2013. Jag skyller på Dr. Deepa Apte — den mjuka, tysttalande läkaren som blev ayurviedisk massör och smorde hela min kropp med doftande sesamolja i en timme — ett ärligt ursäkt. Två tredjedelar in på min förnöjsamma session på hennes massagebord glidde mitt medvetande in i det mest lyckliga tillståndet av sömn — och, precis som kroppsdelar ofta gör när man somnar, spasmade min lår och sparkade den goda läkaren i ansiktet. Det är ett bevis på kraften i hennes tröstande händer och perfekta teknik att jag lyckades lämna alla livets stress vid dörren till hennes dagsspa i North Greenwich och somna så helt och hållet. Ayurveda Pura, ett prispkrönt wellnesscenter, tillämpar ayurveda — ett 5 000 år gammalt indiskt helhetsläkemedel vars namn betyder 'livets vetenskap'. Det strävar efter fysisk och mentalt harmoni med naturen genom kost, yoga, massage, avgiftning, växelrådsmediciner, meditation och dagliga livsstilspraxis. Med andra ord: massager är nödvändiga. Det här är min typ av tro. Som Dr. Deepa förklarade i hennes svalt doftande rum, ser ayurveda allt i universum — inklusive människor — som sammansatt av fem grundläggande element: rum, luft, eld, vatten och jord. Sjukdom, enligt ayurveda, uppstår från en obalans mellan dessa element i en persons konstitution. Behandlingen syftar till att återställa harmoni och återfå hälsan. Dessa element kombinerar till tre doshas: Vata (luft + rum), Pitta (eld + vatten) och Kapha (vatten + jord). Alla har alla tre, men den dominerande kombinationen definierar en persons unika Prakriti, eller konstitutionstyp. Efter att ha hållit min handled och fastställt min kroppstyp — Vata-Pitta: ambitiös, hårt arbetande, hungrig, medelbyggd, ofta med ett gap mellan tänderna (alla ganska exakt) — lade Dr. Deepa mig på hennes mjuka bord. I motsats till djupvävnadsmassager, svenska massager eller sportmassager — som fokuserar på tryck, ledkrock och tvångsrörelser — är en ayurviedisk massage en mjukare, flytande, djupt sensorisk upplevelse. I stället för att hacka knutar, smorde hon min hud med ätbart, kryddinfuserat olja (i ayurveda används ingenting på huden som inte är säkert att äta) och svepte sina handflator över mig, hennes beröring aldrig brytande kontakten. Tillsammans med den mjuka, plinky-plunky musiken, det varma mörka rummet och det mjuka soffan skickade hennes närvaro mig rakt in i sömn. Därför sparken. När timmen var slut, väckte Dr. Deepa mig försiktigt, gav mig möjlighet att tvätta av oljan (hon hade använt nog för att djupfrysa en hel människa) och hällde upp en frisk herbal te medan jag duschar — för att återhämta och förlänga den lyckliga känslan av lugn och tillfredsställelse. När jag svävade tillbaka ut i Greenwich verkade världen något dämpad, mindre het och inte alls så brådskande. Att göra-lista? Vilken att göra-lista? article_content: Six months after vanishing to join the conflict in Iraq and Syria, 16-year-old Feiz from Sydney’s western suburbs has been located safely in Lebanon and is set to return home with his father — assisted by Australian Federal Police. His friend, 17-year-old Abdullah Elmir, however, remains unaccounted for. Abdullah had told his family he was heading out for a fishing trip, but investigators believe both teens traveled via Turkey, Malaysia, and Thailand before attempting to enter Iraq. Their journey began in June, sparked by what authorities suspect was exposure to extremist online content, including an ISIS video titled 'There Is No Life Without Jihad,' which calls on young Muslims to 'wake up and join the effort.' While Feiz’s family expressed relief, Abdullah’s parents are devastated, saying they saw no warning signs and never imagined he’d abandon his future — including plans for university — without a word. A cryptic text message left with a friend simply read: 'Tell my mum I’m gone.' The Australian government has since tightened laws, making it a crime punishable by up to 25 years to support terrorist organizations. Attorney General George Brandis recently noted that roughly 60 Australians are believed to be fighting in Syria, mostly with anti-government factions linked to Al-Qaeda, and another 150 are under surveillance domestically. Although a recent suicide bombing in Iraq was claimed by an Australian extremist named Abu Bakr Al Australi, local community leaders and Abdullah’s family strongly reject any connection between him and the attack. With no Australian embassy in Iraq or Syria, officials face severe limitations in helping citizens trapped in the region.

Hans vän, den 17-årige Abdullah Elmir, finns dock kvar obekant. Abdullah hade sagt till sin familj att han skulle ut på fiske, men undersökare tror att båda tonåringarna reste via Turkiet, Malaysia och Thailand innan de försökte komma över gränsen till Irak. Resan började i juni, utlöst av vad myndigheter misstänker var exponering för extremister på nätet, inklusive ett ISIS-video med titeln 'Det finns inget liv utan jihad', som uppmanar unga muslimer att 'vakna upp och delta i insatsen.' Justitieminister George Brandis noterade nyligen att cirka 60 australier antas vara i Syrien och kämpa främst för anti-regeringsgrupper kopplade till Al-Qaida, och ytterligare 150 är under övervakning i landet. Även om ett nyligen inträffat självmordsattacker i Irak påstås ha utförts av den australiensiska extremismen Abu Bakr Al Australi, avvisar lokala samhällsförträdare och Abdullahs familj starkt någon koppling mellan honom och anslaget. Med ingen australisk ambassad i Irak eller Syrien står myndigheterna inför allvarliga begränsningar när det gäller att hjälpa medborgare som fastnat i regionen.

article_content: In Saint Petersburg, 29-year-old make-up artist Vadim Andreev is turning heads — not with scalpels, but with brushes and palettes. His mission? To prove that stunning transformations don’t require surgery. With nothing but cosmetics, he helps women — and even men — rediscover confidence by enhancing their natural features. What started as a childhood hobby has blossomed into a career where he’s worked with Russian TV stars, models, and everyday brides alike. Vadim’s signature style? Subtle yet powerful. He uses lightweight under-eye concealer to brighten tired eyes, soft cream blush to add warmth to the cheeks, and a touch of highlighter to catch the light just right. Bronzer sculpted along the jawline and cheekbones adds dimension, while black mascara and a hint of warm pink gloss complete the look — fresh, youthful, and effortlessly radiant. He’s documented hundreds of before-and-after shots on his website, vadimandreev.com, not to sell perfection, but to show possibility. One standout case involved a friend from a quiet town, stuck in an outdated style with a heavy fringe. Vadim gave her hair extensions, shaped her brows, applied makeup — and within hours, she walked out feeling like a different person. She kept the look on for three days straight. While a few images get minor digital tweaks — maybe removing stray hairs or adjusting contrast — Vadim insists most results are 100% real. 'It’s not about hiding who you are,' he says. 'It’s about helping people see what’s already there.' He doesn’t limit his art to women. Men seeking a bold gothic edge or simply clearer skin also benefit from his touch. His goal? To remind everyone that beauty isn’t reserved for the privileged or the surgically altered. It’s a skill — one that anyone can learn. Through free tutorials, paid masterclasses, and workshops, Vadim teaches practical, everyday tricks: less is more. No need for thick layers. Just smart placement. He dreams of writing a book and launching his own makeover TV show — but for now, he’s busy changing lives, one brushstroke at a time.

article_content: Lagos, Nigeria (CNN) — The spokesman for the Nigerian militant group Boko Haram has been captured following a months-long surveillance operation, according to a Nigerian police spokesperson on Wednesday. Security services tracked Abu Qa Qa through his mobile phone, despite his frequent changes of location and phone number. Authorities are now working to verify his true identity, though they believe he is a Nigerian citizen. Boko Haram has carried out multiple bombings and shootings across northern Nigeria in recent days. Depending on the faction, the group’s goals range from enforcing strict Islamic Sharia law to overthrowing the government. Abu Qa Qa has been instrumental in connecting journalists with Boko Haram and amplifying its messages on social media — a significant shift given the group’s previous rejection of Western technology. His arrest has provided a much-needed boost to Nigerian security forces, which had faced intense criticism for failing to prevent the January 20 bombings in Kano that killed 211 people. The attacks targeted eight government sites in Nigeria’s second-largest city, reducing police headquarters and other buildings to charred ruins. In response, President Goodluck Jonathan dismissed the country’s inspector general of police. Boko Haram — whose name translates to 'Western education is sacrilege' — claimed responsibility for the blasts in a phone call to the Daily Trust, according to journalists at the newspaper. On Wednesday, Amnesty International further criticized Nigeria’s police response, accusing the force of being 'poorly trained and ill-equipped' and of committing extrajudicial killings and other abuses in retaliation for Boko Haram’s attacks. 'Boko Haram has committed numerous human rights abuses and shows contempt for life,' Amnesty stated. 'But security forces have failed to prevent, investigate, prosecute, or punish these acts — and have often committed new human rights violations with impunity.' Suspected Boko Haram members have been detained without trial, and innocent women and children have been held to extract information about male relatives suspected of involvement, the group reported. 'Investigations into crimes, if they occur, are often inadequate and not intelligence-led,' Amnesty added. CNN repeatedly requested comment from the Nigerian government regarding allegations of extrajudicial killings but received no official response. Civilians have also voiced fears. In an audio-only interview, the mother of a missing man and his pregnant wife told CNN she was too afraid to speak on camera. She described how security forces fired on their home, scattering her son’s Quran and leaving blood pooled by the bedroom door. Despite repeated inquiries, no authorities have confirmed whether her son and daughter-in-law are alive. 'My son is not a member of Boko Haram,' she said. 'If there had been justice, they would have arrested him and brought him before a court. This is jungle justice.' Boko Haram was founded in 2002 by Islamic preacher Mohammed Yusuf, emerging from ethnic and religious tensions in Nigeria during the 1990s. Nigeria’s population is divided between a predominantly Muslim north and a largely Christian south. Yusuf advocated for nationwide implementation of Sharia law and rejected democracy. The group operated openly in northeastern Nigeria until 2009, when police launched a crackdown. Harsh tactics sparked an armed uprising; Yusuf was arrested and later died in custody. His death galvanized Boko Haram to launch attacks on police stations, leading to hundreds of deaths in subsequent clashes.
translated_content: Lagos, Nigeria (CNN) — Sprekläggaren för den nigerianska militanta gruppen Boko Haram har arresterats efter en månader lång övervakningsoperation, enligt en polisspråkförare på onsdag. Säkerhetstjänsterna spårade Abu Qa Qa genom hans mobiltelefon trots att han regelbundet ändrade plats och telefonnummer. Myndigheterna försöker nu verifiera hans riktiga identitet, även om de tror att han är en nigeriansk medborgare. Boko Haram har utfört flera bombattacker och skottlossningar i norra Nigeria under de senaste dagarna. Beroende på fraktionen strävar gruppen antingen efter strikt genomförande av islamsk Sharia-lag eller övergripande förstöring av regeringen. Abu Qa Qa har varit avgörande för att koppla samman journalister med Boko Haram och sprida dess budskap på sociala medier — en betydande förändring givet gruppen tidigare avvisande hållning mot västlig teknik. Hans arrestering har gett säkerhetstjänsterna ett mycket behövt uppsving, som tidigare kritiserats för att ha misslyckats med att förhindra bombattackerna den 20 januari i Kano, där 211 personer dödades. Anfallen riktades mot åtta regeringsbyggnader i Nigerias näst största stad och lämnade polishuvudkontoret och andra byggnader till förstörda ruiner. I svar på detta avskedade president Goodluck Jonathan landets polischef. Boko Haram — vars namn översätts till 'Västerländsk utbildning är helgonförakt' — tog ansvar för bombningarna i ett telefonsamtal till Daily Trust, enligt journalister vid tidningen. Onsdag kritiserade Amnesty International ytterligare den nigerianska polisens respons och beskrev den som 'dåligt utbildad och otillräckligt utrustad' och anklagade den för att begå extrajudiciella dödanden och andra överträdelser som hämnd för Boko Harams attacker. 'Boko Haram har begått många människorättskränkningar och visar förakt för liv', sa Amnesty. 'Men säkerhetsstyrkorna har misslyckats med att förhindra, undersöka, åtal eller bestraffa dessa handlingar — och har ofta begått nya människorättskränkningar med impunitet.' Misstänkta Boko Haram-medlemmar har hållits i fängelse utan rättegång, och oskyldiga kvinnor och barn har hållts fångna för att få information om män i deras familjer som misstänks för brott, uppger gruppen. 'Utredningar av brott, om de sker, är ofta otillräckliga och inte baserade på underrättelser', sa Amnesty. CNN har upprepade gånger begärt kommentar från den nigerianska regeringen angående anklagelser om extrajudiciella dödanden men har inte fått något officiellt svar. Civilpersoner har också uttryckt rädsla. I ett ljudbaserat intervju berättade modern till en försvunnen man och hans gravida hustru för CNN att hon var för rädd för att tala på kamera. Hon beskrev hur säkerhetsstyrkor sköt mot deras hem, spridde hennes sons Koran och lämnade blod som samlats vid sovrumsdörren. Trots upprepade förfrågningar har ingen myndighet bekräftat om hennes son och svärson är levande. 'Min son är inte medlem i Boko Haram', sa hon. 'Om det hade funnits rättvisa skulle de ha arresterat honom och fört honom inför en domstol. Detta är jungeldomstol.' Boko Haram grundades 2002 av den islamiske predikanten Mohammed Yusuf, som utvecklades ur etniska och religiösa spänningar i Nigeria under 1990-talet. Nigerias befolkning är uppdelad mellan ett övervägande muslimska norr och ett övervägande kristet söder. Yusuf förespråkade införande av Sharia-lag i hela norra regionen och avvisade demokrati. Gruppen opererade öppet i nordöstra Nigeria fram till 2009, då polisen lanserade ett nedslag. Hårda metoder utlöste ett vapenuppror; Yusuf greps och dog senare i polisförvar. Hans död mobiliserade Boko Haram att starta attacker mot polisstationer, vilket ledde till hundratals dödade i efterföljande kamp.

article_content: A talented three-year-old has become the youngest-ever competitor at the Horse of the Year Show, riding his pony Divine at the national event in Birmingham. Harry Edwards-Brady, who began riding just months ago, competed in the rein-led pony discipline before thousands of spectators at the Birmingham NEC arena. He qualified for the finals after earning a near-perfect score of 48 out of 50 at the Royal Norfolk Show in May. Despite being only three years old—and riding a four-year-old pony, the minimum age allowed—Harry finished seventh out of 28 competitors, many of whom were more than three times his age. His mother, Emma Edwards-Brady from Hatherleigh, Devon, said, 'He did amazing—the pony rode so well, and we couldn’t ask for more. To finish seventh with the youngest competitor and the youngest pony isn’t a bad result at all.' Harry has already won four 'Best Rider' titles at local shows and is gaining recognition as a rising talent in equestrian sports.

Han kvalificerade sig till finalen efter att ha fått nästan perfekt poäng — 48 av 50 — vid Royal Norfolk Show i maj. Trots att han bara är tre år gammal — och rider en fyra år gammal ponny, vilket är den yngsta tillåtna åldern — avslutade Harry på sjunde plats bland 28 deltagare, många av vilka var mer än tre gånger hans ålder. Hans mor, Emma Edwards-Brady från Hatherleigh i Devon, sa: 'Han gjorde fantastiskt — ponyn red så bra, och vi kunde inte önska mer. Att komma på sjunde plats med den yngsta tävlande och den yngsta ponnyen är inte ett dåligt resultat alls.' article_content: Rome (CNN) — The new pope offered insight into his choice of the name Francis during an audience with journalists on Saturday, expressing his desire for a Church that is both poor and 'for the poor.' His remarks came during his first media appearance since becoming the first Jesuit and first Latin American to lead the Roman Catholic Church three days earlier. Francis, formerly known as Cardinal Jorge Bergoglio, said a fellow cardinal from Brazil reminded him, 'Don’t forget the poor,' as votes accumulated in his favor. That phrase stayed with him, he recalled, as it became clear he had secured the two-thirds majority needed to become pope. 'Right away, concerning the poor, I thought of St. Francis of Assisi; then I thought of war,' he told journalists. 'Francis loved peace — and that’s how the name came to me.' He also reflected on St. Francis’s deep concern for the environment and his life as a 'poor and simple man' — ideals he hopes the Church embodies. St. Francis of Assisi, who renounced wealth and status, is revered by Catholics for his service to the poor. The gathering included Vatican communications staff and several Latin American reporters, mostly from Argentina. Francis began by thanking them for covering the historic events following Pope Benedict XVI’s unexpected resignation. He drew a parallel between journalism and the Church’s mission, noting both strive to convey 'truth, beauty, and goodness.' He acknowledged the media’s vital role in explaining the Church’s workings — complicated by its foundation in faith rather than politics. Closing the audience — which included no questions — he offered a blessing to all present and their families, adding, 'I give you my blessing knowing you belong to different religions, because all of you are children of God.' As cardinal in Buenos Aires, Francis cultivated close ties with Argentina’s Jewish community. This week, he wrote to the chief rabbi in Rome, expressing hope to 'contribute to the progress of relations between Jews and Catholics' since the Second Vatican Council, 'in a spirit of renewed collaboration.' On Sunday, he will celebrate Mass in Vatican City and deliver his first Angelus blessing from the window of his papal apartment to crowds in St. Peter’s Square. The official Mass inaugurating him as Bishop of Rome — and leader of the world’s 1.2 billion Catholics — takes place Tuesday. Observers have noted his humble style since election, sparking speculation about broader reforms. The Vatican announced Saturday that current heads of Vatican departments will remain in place for now, with no definitive appointments made. CNN Vatican analyst John Allen notes this departure from tradition signals possible imminent change: 'It’s customary for new popes to quickly reconfirm department heads and delay their own appointments. The fact that Francis has not followed that path may suggest significant personnel moves are coming sooner rather than later.' The Vatican stated Francis seeks 'a certain period for reflection, prayer, and dialogue' before making any nominations. The media audience came one day after the Vatican dismissed allegations regarding Francis’s conduct during Argentina’s Dirty War, accusing him of failing to protect two kidnapped Jesuit priests. Vatican spokesman Father Federico Lombardi called the claims 'defamatory and untrue,' emphasizing that Bergoglio was never charged, only questioned as a witness, and had documented evidence of protecting victims. Francis is scheduled to meet his predecessor, Pope Emeritus Benedict XVI, on March 23 at Castel Gandolfo, where Benedict has resided since his resignation. While some worry a living ex-pope might cause confusion or influence, the Vatican insists Benedict will focus solely on prayer and study, with no role in governance. CNN’s Hada Messia reported from Rome; Laura Smith-Spark wrote and reported from London.
translated_content: Rome (CNN) — Den nya påven gav insikt i sitt val av namnet Franciskus vid ett möte med journalister på lördag och uttryckte sin önskan om en kyrka som är både fattig och 'för de fattiga.' Hans kommentarer kom under hans första mediauppträdande sedan han blev den förste jesuiten och den första latinamerikanske ledaren för den romersk-katolska kyrkan för tre dagar sedan. Franciskus, tidigare känd som kardinal Jorge Bergoglio, sa att en kollega från Brasilien påminde honom om 'Glöm inte de fattiga' när rösterna ackumulerades till hans förmån. Den frasen stannade hos honom, minns han, när det blev tydligt att han fått den två tredjedelars majoritet som krävdes för att bli påve. 'Omedelbart, angående de fattiga, tänkte jag på Sankt Franciskus av Assisi; sedan tänkte jag på krig,' sa han till journalister. 'Franciskus älskade fred — och så kom namnet till mig.' Han reflekterade också över Sankt Franciskus djupa oro för miljön och hans liv som en 'fattig och enkel man' — ideal som han hoppas kyrkan ska inkarnera. Sankt Franciskus av Assisi, som avstod från rikedom och status, hyllas av katoliker för sitt tjänande till de fattiga. Mötet inkluderade Vatikanens kommunikationspersonal och flera latinamerikanska journalister, främst från Argentina. Franciskus började med att tacka dem för att de täckte de historiska händelserna efter påve Benedikt XVI:s oväntade avgång. Han drog en parallell mellan journalistik och kyrkans uppdrag, och noterade att båda strävar efter att förmedla 'sanning, skönhet och godhet.' Han erkände journalisternas viktiga roll att förklara kyrkans funktioner — komplicerade av dess grund i tro snarare än politik. Vid avslutningen av mötet — som inte inkluderade frågor — gav han en välsignelse till alla närvarande och deras familjer, och tillade: 'Jag ger er min välsignelse med vetskap om att ni tillhör olika religioner, eftersom alla ni är Guds barn.' Som kardinal i Buenos Aires utvecklade Franciskus nära band med Argentinas judiska gemenskap. Denna vecka skrev han till huvudrabbinen i Rom och uttryckte hoppet om att 'bidra till utvecklingen av relationerna mellan judar och katoliker' sedan Andra Vatikankonciliet på 1960-talet, 'i en anda av förnyad samverkan.' Söndag kommer han att firar messa i Vatikanen och hålla sin första Angelusvälsignelse från fönstret till sin päpstliga lägenhet till folkmassorna i Sankt Petri-kyrkoplan. Den officiella messan som införde honom som biskop av Rom — och ledare för världens 1,2 miljarder katoliker — äger rum tisdag. Observatörer har noterat hans enkla stil sedan valet, vilket väckt spekulationer om bredare reformer. Vatikanen meddelade på lördag att nuvarande chefer för Vatikanens avdelningar kommer att behålla sina jobb för tillfället, utan några definitiva utsedningar. CNN:s Vatikananalysör John Allen noterar att denna avvikelse från traditionen antyder möjliga snabba förändringar: 'Det är vanligt att nya påvar snabbt bekräftar departementschefer och dröjer med att utseda sina egna. Att Francis inte följt den vägen kan tyda på att betydande personalförändringar kommer snabbare än senare.' Vatikanen säger att Francis söker 'en viss period för reflektion, bön och dialog' innan han gör några utsedningar. Medieuppträdandet kom en dag efter att Vatikanen avvisat anklagelser om Franciskus roll under Argentinas 'Skitkrig', där han anklagades för att ha misslyckats med att skydda två jesuitpräster som blivit kidnapplade. Vatikanens talesman, pater Federico Lombardi, kallade påståendena 'förolämpande och osanna', och betonade att Bergoglio aldrig åtalats, endast förhörs som vittne, och hade dokumenterad bevisning för att ha skyddat offer. Franciskus är schemalagd att möta sin företrädare, Pape Emeritus Benedikt XVI, den 23 mars i Castel Gandolfo, där Benedict bott sedan sin historiska avgång. Även om vissa oroas för att en levande tidigare påve skulle kunna orsaka förvirring eller inflytande, insisterar Vatikanen på att Benedikt kommer att fokusera enbart på bön och studier, utan någon roll i ledningen.

He emphasized the Pacific Islanders’ physicality, pride, and raw passion, drawing parallels to Fiji’s near-victory over Wales just days earlier. George Ford returns at fly-half, while longtime friend Owen Farrell shifts to inside centre, reuniting in a partnership that once served England well at age group level. Ben Youngs takes over at scrum-half, Rob Webber gets the nod at hooker following Dylan Hartley’s red card, and veteran James Haskell returns to the back row alongside Ben Morgan, replacing the out-of-form Tom Wood and Billy Vunipola. Lancaster acknowledged the team’s recent decline, particularly in the loose forwards, and believes Haskell’s carrying ability and leadership will provide much-needed energy. article_content: From midnight last night, the UK’s exclusive rights to sell Viagra ended, opening the floodgates for cheaper generic alternatives. What once cost up to £6 per pill could soon drop to just 60p — a 90% price cut that’s set to transform how men access treatment for erectile dysfunction. But here’s the catch: you still need a prescription. Whether you’re getting it through the NHS or paying out-of-pocket, a doctor’s approval remains mandatory. Around two dozen pharmaceutical firms are now rolling out their own versions of the drug, all containing the same active ingredient — sildenafil. Pfizer, the original creator, isn’t stepping aside; it’s joining the race with its own unbranded sildenafil tablets. Leading the charge among generics is Teva, a giant in NHS drug supply, known for everything from cough syrup to chemotherapy meds. Their spokesperson joked they’re racing like cats and dogs to be first off the blocks when patents expire. The new pills won’t look like the classic blue diamond — they’ll come in different shapes, colors, and sizes — but they’ll work just as effectively. For the NHS, this shift could mean saving tens of millions annually, especially since it currently spends over £40 million on Viagra alone. The real winners? The roughly 150,000 people who pay full price privately — they’ve been shelling out around £24 for four tablets. Now, experts like Paul Fleming from the British Generic Manufacturers Association are urging them to ask their doctors to prescribe ‘sildenafil’ instead of ‘Viagra’ — that’s where the savings kick in. Currently, the NHS only covers Viagra for men with conditions like diabetes or prostate cancer. But with costs plummeting, some hope eligibility rules might eventually widen. Dr Mike Wyllie, one of Viagra’s original developers, believes cheaper legal options will kill off the dangerous black-market counterfeit trade. ‘This isn’t just about money,’ he said. ‘It’s about giving people safe, affordable access to a treatment that improves quality of life.’

article_content: Hundreds of Britain’s top A-level students are opting to study abroad, driven by rising tuition costs and compelling international alternatives. In 2012, around 600 students who achieved three A or A* grades chose not to enroll at UK universities. Many are now reapplying, while others have secured places at prestigious institutions in Europe and the United States — including Ivy League schools like Harvard, Yale, and Stanford — drawn by lower fees and enhanced career prospects. The introduction of £9,000 annual tuition fees in the UK in 2012 shifted student preferences. At Sevenoaks School in Kent, one in four sixth-formers applied to US universities this year. Last year, several rejected offers from Oxford and Cambridge to attend Stanford, the University of Pennsylvania, and Yale instead. Headmistress Katy Ricks noted, 'The top end of our range are looking globally. It is no longer a given that they’ll choose the British option.' European universities are also seeing a surge in UK applicants. Maastricht University in the Netherlands, which offers English-taught degrees for just £1,600 per year, reported an 80% increase in British students over the past year. According to the Times Higher Education global rankings, Oxford and Cambridge remain the only UK universities in the top 10. However, institutions like Edinburgh and Imperial College London still rank within the top 50. Meanwhile, recent data from UCAS shows that for the first time in a decade, the proportion of UK students entering university with top A-level grades has declined relative to those with slightly lower scores. Professor Sir Steve Smith, Chair of UCAS, expressed concern: 'It would be genuinely worrying if a trend developed where large numbers of top students opt for universities outside the UK. That would be of great concern.'

article_content: On a chilly Saturday afternoon in New York, Bob Votruba stands outside the school bus he calls home. At 58, the retired father of three lives on just 84 square feet — a space he describes as 'pure luxury' and 'a little sacred.' For the past four years, Votruba has been traveling across the U.S. in his converted bus, covering nearly 60,000 miles on a mission to inspire 'One Million Acts of Kindness.' His loyal companion, Bogart, a Boston terrier, rides beside him. His journey began after the 2007 Virginia Tech shooting, which prompted deep introspection. Feeling unfulfilled by his former life in construction and watching his children leave for college, he sought purpose beyond comfort. He traveled to Virginia Tech the week after the tragedy, listening to survivors and families — an experience that changed him forever. Upon returning home, he told his children he would sell everything and hit the road to spread kindness. Though surprised, they were not shocked. 'Dad was always kind,' said his daughter Lizzie, 23. 'We’re proud he’s doing what he believes is right,' added son Peter, 25. April 16 — the date of the Virginia Tech massacre — remains deeply personal to Votruba. Yet, when he shared its significance with a local chamber group in Ohio, many faces remained blank. 'Events fade from public memory,' he laments. 'We live in a Post-it note society — we need constant reminders to care.' To stay grounded, Votruba sets four daily alarms to pause and reflect on how he can be kinder. He believes small gestures — holding a door, smiling, letting someone merge in traffic — build habits of compassion. He drives to towns with mild weather, visiting schools and senior centers to distribute flyers. Some organizations invite him back months or even years later. Two years ago, he added a bicycle to his travels, riding nearly 18,000 miles while displaying messages like 'Be a man. Don’t raise a hand. Stop domestic violence' and 'Stop childhood sexual abuse now.' Children often respond to the sign above his handlebars: 'Boys should never hit girls.' He hears raw stories: parents grieving lost children, adults crying decades after childhood trauma, strangers sharing suicide losses. To honor them, he hands out 'kindness certificates' — tangible tokens meant to be framed and remembered. Inside his unheated bus, more than 400 handwritten notes line the walls — from toddlers to centenarians. One child scribbled: 'Just be nice.' A 92-year-old man wrote: 'Tell your love, you love her every day.' Votruba says these words warm his soul, even on the coldest days. Visitors from as far as Australia have stopped by his bus in Brooklyn, leaving messages and sharing stories. 'He radiates joy,' says Sister Claire Young of Florida. 'You say hello, and he beams. What could be better?'

article_content: Graham Wilkinson never expected a parking ticket for simply pausing his van at a zebra crossing while his 12-year-old son stepped out. But that’s exactly what happened. The brief stop — lasting just seven seconds — occurred outside Shoeburyness High School in Southend-on-Sea, as two pupils walked across the road. A council surveillance vehicle, equipped with a rotating CCTV camera, captured the moment, leading to a £35 fine for alleged illegal parking. Wilkinson, a resident of Shoebury, insists he wasn’t parking — he was legally waiting for pedestrians. 'I didn’t pull over to get out,' he said. 'I was already stopped. My son got out because it was safe to do so.' He even consulted a police officer, who confirmed no traffic law was broken. The council’s photo shows his white van halted at the crossing, with his son Joel exiting and children crossing behind him. The incident has ignited broader criticism of Southend Council’s fleet of two 'spy cars' — Toyota iQs fitted with cameras — which have collected nearly half a million pounds in fines since 2011. Critics, including transport operators and civil liberties groups, argue the program is less about safety and more about income. Bill Cook, who runs school transport services, says the fines are making school bus routes unaffordable, with some schools now paying fines themselves to keep buses running. Over 44% of motorists who challenged similar fines through the Traffic Penalty Tribunal had them revoked, suggesting widespread misapplication. Government ministers like Brandon Lewis and Eric Pickles have condemned the practice, calling it a 'money-making scheme' that undermines fairness. Pickles once pledged to ban such vehicles, arguing traffic wardens with cameras could handle enforcement without the public backlash. While the council defends its actions, saying each case is reviewed individually and appeals are accepted, many feel common sense has been lost. As one observer put it: 'It’s not about breaking rules — it’s about understanding context.' With over 100 such vehicles operating across Britain and £30 million in fines collected in a year, the debate isn't just about one family — it's about how far enforcement should go.

Över 44 procent av de bilister som anmält liknande böter genom Traffic Penalty Tribunal fick dem upphävda, vilket tyder på bred missanvändning. Regeringsministrar som Brandon Lewis och Eric Pickles har fördömt praxisen, och kallat den för ett 'pengagörande system' som undergräver rättvisa. Pickles lovade någon gång att förbjuda sådana fordon, och menade att trafikvakter med kameror kunde hantera kontrollen utan offentlig upprördhet. Medan rådet försvarar sina handlingar genom att säga att varje fall granskas individuellt och att invändningar godtas, många känner att sunt förnuft har gått förlorat. Som en observatör uttryckte det: 'Det handlar inte om att bryta regler — det handlar om att förstå sammanhanget.' Med över 100 sådana fordon i drift över Storbritannien och 30 miljoner pund i böter samlade in under ett år, handlar debatten inte bara om en familj — den handlar om hur långt kontrollen ska gå.

article_content: Obesity, heavy drinking, and a sedentary lifestyle are driving rising cancer rates among middle-aged adults, a report warns. The number of people in their 40s and 50s diagnosed with cancer has increased by 20% over the past 30 years. While cancer survival rates have improved—doubling over the last four decades—experts caution that this does not offset growing incidence. Tumors once considered typical in older adults are now increasingly common in younger populations, due to earlier detection through national screening programs, advanced diagnostics, and improved treatments. According to Cancer Research UK, the likelihood of surviving cancer for at least 10 years has nearly doubled to almost 50%. Each year, approximately 61,000 Britons aged 40 to 59 are diagnosed with cancer. Prostate cancer rates in middle-aged men have risen sixfold in three decades, with nearly 4,000 new cases annually. It remains the most common cancer in men, affecting roughly one in nine men over their lifetime. Breast cancer rates among women aged 40–59 have increased by 60% in the same period, with around 17,110 cases each year. One in eight women will develop breast cancer at some point in their lives. Other cancers—including those of the bowel, stomach, kidney, throat, and mouth—are also becoming more prevalent in this age group and are strongly linked to obesity, physical inactivity, and alcohol consumption. Lung cancer is the only major cancer type to have declined significantly in the past 30 years, largely due to reduced smoking rates. Recent data show that 42% of Britons will be diagnosed with cancer during their lifetime—up from 33% a decade ago. Macmillan Cancer Support warns the NHS may struggle to cope with the surge in cases, many tied to unhealthy lifestyles. Research indicates that fat tissue in overweight individuals produces hormones like insulin and estrogen, which can promote tumor growth. Alcohol and diets high in red meat, along with lack of exercise, are also implicated. Experts urge adults in their 40s and 50s to monitor for symptoms and seek prompt medical attention. Sara Hiom, Director of Health Information at Cancer Research UK, said: 'We can reduce our cancer risk by avoiding smoking, limiting alcohol, maintaining a healthy weight, exercising regularly, and eating a balanced diet. Yet, unhealthy choices—like taking the elevator instead of the stairs—are often the easiest.' 'Acting quickly on symptoms, attending screenings when invited, and receiving timely diagnosis and treatment can make a critical difference to long-term survival,' she added. The rise in breast and prostate cancer diagnoses is partly due to improved screening, not just increased incidence. Mike Hobday, Head of Policy at Macmillan Cancer Support, stated: 'It is deeply concerning that cancer rates among middle-aged men and women have risen so rapidly in just one generation. The NHS must recognize cancer as a long-term condition and invest in services that support lifelong management.'

article_content: The fatal shooting of a 13-month-old boy in his stroller marked the second time mother Sherry West had lost a son to violence, she said Saturday. Her 18-year-old son was stabbed to death in New Jersey in 2008, she told CNN. 'This is the second child that people have taken from me in a tragic way,' West said. 'I'm so afraid to have any more babies now. I tried to raise really good kids in a wicked world.' The day after two teenage boys were arrested and charged in connection with the fatal shooting of her baby, West said she planned to leave Brunswick and return to New Jersey. The boy’s father has also been emotionally distraught, West said. Asked about the person who shot her son, Antonio, West stated: 'I hate you, and I don’t forgive you. You killed an innocent human life. I hope you die for it.' A private memorial service was held Friday morning for young Antonio Santiago, who was cremated, according to West. She said the family is working with the Catholic relief organization, the Society of St. Vincent de Paul, to help cover unforeseen expenses. West put Antonio in a stroller Thursday because it was good exercise for her heart, she said, adding that she is disabled due to a past car accident. 'I just took a walk with my baby,' West said. 'I can’t believe this would happen. I left early in the morning—I thought there would be fewer people on the road and I wouldn’t be in anyone’s way.' 'Apparently, either he targeted me, or I was just unfortunate,' she said of her encounter with the gunman. West said the incident occurred at 9 a.m. Thursday as she was walking home from the post office. She saw two boys, and one asked for money. When she told them she didn’t have any, one of the boys shot her in the leg and then her son in the face. Police Chief Tobe Green identified the older suspect as De’Marquise Elkins, 17, and said he will be tried as an adult. The 14-year-old has not been publicly named due to his age. Both have been charged with first-degree murder, police said, though no arraignment date has been set. As of Saturday, authorities had not yet recovered the murder weapon, said police spokesman Todd Rhodes. However, they located the two suspects using West’s description, eyewitness accounts, and school attendance records to identify which students were absent on Thursday. Officers then tracked them down and took them into custody. 911 calls revealed witnesses’ horror. Earlier Saturday, police in the coastal city released three recordings of 911 calls regarding Thursday’s shooting. 'A baby has been shot!' one woman cried in a 911 call. The exchange with the emergency operator was emotionally charged. 'Listen to me, ma’am! Is the baby breathing?' the operator asked. 'I don’t know,' the woman replied. She began to cry. In the background, people could be heard wailing on the corner of London and Ellis Streets, near a cluster of Victorian-style homes with wraparound porches. 'Listen to me!' the operator urged the sobbing woman. 'We have people en route. Did you hear shots in the area?' 'Yes, I heard shots,' she said. 'Be calm,' the operator instructed. 'How many shots did you hear?' 'I heard three shots. And the baby has been shot in the head,' she said. Distraught, the woman handed her phone to a man walking his dog. 'No, the baby is not breathing,' he told the operator. 'The baby was shot in the head?' the operator confirmed. 'Yes, right between the eyes,' the man said, adding he had earlier heard a 'small-caliber clap.' As he spoke, police sirens arrived on the scene, and he ended the call.

Samtalet med nödsentralen var emotionellt uppladdat. 'Lyssna på mig, fru! Andas barnet?' svarade operatören. 'Jag vet inte,' sa kvinnan. Kvinnan började gråta. I bakgrunden hördes allmänhetens skrik på hörnet av London och Ellis Streets, vid en präktig samling victorianska hus med verandor. 'Lyssna på mig!' sa operatören till den gråtande kvinnan. Och barnet har blivit skjutet i huvudet,' sa kvinnan. Kvinnan var så chockad att hon överlämnade sin mobil till en man som gick sin hund. 'Nej, barnet andas inte,' sa mannen till operatören. 'Barnet blev skjutet i huvudet?' fortsatte operatören. 'Ja, rakt mellan ögonen,' sa mannen, som tillade att han tidigare hört ett 'liten kaliberknap.' Medan han talade ankom polissirener till platsen, och mannen avslutade samtalet.

article_content: ALPHARETTA, Georgia (CNN) — Ben, a 15-month-old golden retriever, can already do many things: turn on lights, open doors, pick up a remote control, and even pull heavy objects with his teeth. Colise Johnson, 42, spent two weeks in September at a canine training camp to bond with Ben. But Ben isn’t just a family pet—he’s a specially trained seizure response dog who may one day save Johnson’s life. ‘Having epilepsy and cerebral palsy is like living on a nonstop roller coaster,’ said Johnson, of Portland, Oregon. ‘You never know what’s coming—but with Ben, he slows the ride down so it’s manageable.’ Johnson, who uses a wheelchair and wears a helmet due to frequent seizures, is one of 3 million Americans living with epilepsy—a neurological disorder causing recurrent seizures, violent muscle spasms, or loss of consciousness. There are no reliable estimates of how many people with epilepsy are partnered with assistance dogs, and scientific research on their benefits remains limited. However, Dr. Gregory Barkley, a neurologist at Henry Ford Hospital in Detroit and adviser to the Epilepsy Foundation of America, believes nearly a quarter of those with frequent, severe seizures could benefit from a canine companion. He emphasizes that these dogs offer crucial emotional support through their unwavering loyalty. Contrary to popular belief, Barkley clarifies, ‘The dog does not predict a seizure. It responds to early physical changes during the onset.’ Johnson previously owned a seizure dog named McKeever for 12 years until his death in 2007—ironically, from a seizure. ‘He alerted me before seizures happened,’ she recalled. ‘He helped me get up if I fell, retrieved items, fetched clothes for bathing, opened the fridge on command, and even took out the recycling.’ After McKeever’s passing, Johnson felt lost—until she was matched with Ben at Canine Assistants in Alpharetta, Georgia. This year, she was one of 1,100 people on the organization’s waiting list. Founded in 1991 by Jennifer Arnold, Canine Assistants has placed over 1,000 service dogs with adults and children with physical disabilities, including muscular dystrophy, multiple sclerosis, cerebral palsy, and brain injuries. In recent years, the nonprofit has trained about 100 seizure response dogs specifically for people with epilepsy. ‘We train them to perform roughly 90 commands,’ Arnold said. ‘That includes going for help, pressing emergency buttons to call 9-1-1, and staying calm during a seizure.’ Over time, nearly all the dogs develop the ability to sense when a seizure is approaching. ‘We don’t yet understand what triggers their awareness—is it a scent? A change in breathing? We’re still figuring it out,’ Arnold explained. Dogs are conditioned to recognize seizure behaviors without becoming frightened. Some can detect warning signs 20 to 40 minutes in advance. ‘When they sense a seizure is coming, they become restless and visibly distressed,’ Arnold said. ‘If their human learns to read those signals, it becomes a powerful early-warning system.’ Barkley notes that while some untrained family pets have shown similar behaviors, formal training greatly increases reliability. He warns against agencies that charge exorbitant fees for dogs whose abilities are unverified. Canine Assistants provides its dogs free of charge—including airfare, lodging during training, and lifetime food and veterinary care—valued at approximately $20,000 per dog. A third of its operating budget comes from corporate grants; the rest is funded by private donations. Arnold, who personally trained many of the 140 dogs currently at the facility, says letting them go is never hard. ‘For many of these people, having epilepsy makes them feel like prisoners in their own homes,’ she said. ‘They’re afraid to leave. But with a dog, they’re never alone.’ Johnson, a married mother of a 15-year-old, is eager to regain independence. ‘Ben will give my family a break,’ she said. ‘They’ll finally be able to rest.’ More than that, she looks forward to joy again. ‘Instead of sinking into sadness over seizures, I’ll play with Ben, laugh with him—and start each day with purpose.’ 'These dogs don’t just change your life—they redefine it. Once you’ve had one, you can’t imagine how you ever lived without them.'
translated_content: ALPHARETTA, Georgia (CNN) — Ben, en 15 månader gammal guldretor, kan redan göra många saker: slå på ljus, öppna dörrar, plocka upp en fjärrkontroll och till och med dra tunga föremål med tänderna. Colise Johnson, 42, tillbringade två veckor i september på en hundträningstävling för att bonding med Ben. Men Ben är inte bara en husdjur — han är en särskilt utbildad epilepsihund som kanske en dag kommer att rädda Johnsons liv. ‘Att ha epilepsi och cerebral pares är som att leva på en oavbruten bergbana,’ sa Johnson från Portland, Oregon. ‘Du vet aldrig vad som kommer — men med Ben saktar han ner färden så den blir hanterbar.’ Johnson, som använder en rullstol och bär en hjälm på grund av frekventa anfall, är en av 3 miljoner amerikaner som lever med epilepsi — ett neurologiskt tillstånd som orsakar återkommande anfall, våldsamma muskelkrampar eller ibland medvetandeförlust. Det finns inga pålitliga uppskattningar om hur många personer med epilepsi har fått assistanshundar, och vetenskaplig forskning om deras fördelar är begränsad. Men Dr. Gregory Barkley, neurolog vid Henry Ford Hospital i Detroit och rådgivare för Epilepsifonden i Amerika, tror att nästan en fjärdedel av de som har frekventa, allvarliga anfall skulle kunna profitera av en hundkompis. Han betonar att dessa hundar erbjuder avgörande emotionellt stöd genom sin oföränderliga lojalitet. Till skillnad från det populära tron, förtydligar Barkley: ‘Hunden förutspår inte ett anfall. Den reagerar på tidiga fysiska förändringar under början.’ Johnson hade tidigare en epilepsihund som hette McKeever i 12 år tills han dog 2007 — ironiskt nog av ett anfall. ‘Han varnade mig innan anfallen kom,’ minns hon. ‘Han hjälpte mig att komma upp om jag föll, hämtade saker, tog fram kläder till badet, öppnade kylskåpet på kommando och till och med tog ut soporna.’ Efter McKeavers död kände Johnson sig förlorad — tills hon fick Ben hos Canine Assistants i Alpharetta, Georgia. Det här året var hon en av 1 100 personer på organisationens väntelista. Grundad 1991 av Jennifer Arnold, har Canine Assistants placerat över 1 000 servicehundar hos vuxna och barn med fysiska funktionsnedsättningar, inklusive muskeldystrofi, multipel skleros, cerebral pares och hjärnskador. Under de senaste åren har den ideella organisationen utbildat cirka 100 epilepsihundar specifikt för personer med epilepsi. ‘Vi tränar dem att utföra ungefär 90 kommandon,’ säger Arnold. ‘Det inkluderar att hämta hjälp, trycka på nödknappar för att ringa 9-1-1 och hålla sig lugna under ett anfall.’ Med tiden utvecklar nästan alla hundarna förmågan att känna av när ett anfall är på väg. ‘Vi förstår ännu inte vad som utlöser deras medvetenhet — är det en luktsignal? En förändring i andningen? Vi är fortfarande på gång att ta reda på det,’ förklarar Arnold. Hundarna tränas att känna igen anfallsbeteenden utan att bli rädda. Vissa kan upptäcka varningstecken 20 till 40 minuter i förväg. ‘När de känner att ett anfall kommer, blir de oroliga och synligt oroliga,’ säger Arnold. ‘Om deras människa lär sig läsa dessa signaler blir det ett kraftfullt varningssystem.’ Barkley noterar att några otränade hushundar visat liknande beteenden, men formell träning ökar pålitligheten avsevärt. Han varnar mot organisationer som kräver höga avgifter för hundar vars förmågor inte är verifierade. Canine Assistants ger sina hundar kostnadsfritt — inklusive flygresor, boende under träningen och livslång mat och veterinärvård — med ett uppskattat värde på cirka 20 000 dollar per hund. En tredjedel av dess driftkostnader täcks av stora bolagsdonationer; resten samlas in genom privata donationer. Arnold, som själv tränat många av de 140 hundarna som för närvarande finns i anläggningen, säger att det aldrig är svårt att släppa loss dem. ‘För många av dessa människor gör epilepsi dem till fångar i sina egna hem,’ säger hon. ‘De är rädda för att lämna huset. Men med en hund är de aldrig ensamma.’ Johnson, en gift mor till en 15-åring, ser fram emot att återfå sin självständighet. ‘Ben kommer att ge min familj en paus,’ säger hon. ‘De kommer äntligen kunna vila.’ Mer än så, hoppas hon på glädje igen. ‘Istället för att sjunka ner i sorg över anfallen, kommer jag att leka med Ben, skratta med honom — och börja varje dag med syfte.’ 'Dessa hundar förändrar inte bara ditt liv — de odefinierar det. När du en gång har en, kan du inte föreställa dig hur du någonsin levde utan den.'

article_content: On New Year’s Day, the body of 25-year-old Ting Fang was discovered in a hotel room in Adelaide, her throat severely injured. Authorities determined she had been killed by multiple cuts to her jugular veins. The suspect, 27-year-old Chungaung Piao—a Chinese national living in Australia under a bridging visa—was charged with her murder. Piao, who resides in Adelaide’s western suburb of Allenby Gardens and is a father to an eight-month-old child, initially sought release on home detention bail. However, after the prosecution presented compelling evidence—including his fingerprint found on Fang’s shoe—he withdrew his application. His lawyer, Julian Kelly, confirmed the withdrawal, noting that Piao had voluntarily gone to the police station and maintained his innocence, arguing the fingerprint could align with his account of contact with the victim. The discovery of Fang’s body came when flooding from a running tap in her room alerted hotel staff. Police believe she had been in Adelaide for several days prior to her death and was engaged in sex work. The case was adjourned by Magistrate Luke Davis until March 31, leaving open the possibility of a future bail request.

Piao, som bor i Adelaides västra förort Allenby Gardens och är far till ett åtta månader gammalt barn, sökte först frigivning på hemkvarnsbetingad villkorlig frigivning. Men efter att åklagaren presenterade övertygande bevis – inklusive hans fingeravtryck på Fangs sko – drog han tillbaka ansökan. Hans advokat, Julian Kelly, bekräftade tillbakadragandet och noterade att Piao själv gått till polisen och bibehållit sin oskuld, och att fingeravtrycket kan sammanfalla med hans version om kontakt med offeret. Kroppen upptäcktes när översvämning från en öppen kran i rummet larmade hotellpersonal. Polisen tror att hon varit i Adelaide i flera dagar innan hon dödades och att hon arbetade som säljerska. article_content: Julie Bailey, a café owner and mother of two, founded the campaign group 'Cure the NHS' after her mother Bella died in 2007 under appalling conditions at Mid Staffordshire Hospital. Her advocacy helped uncover a systemic crisis: between 2005 and 2008, up to 1,200 patients may have died needlessly due to neglect. In recent developments, Roy 'Murph' Guest, a senior call handler for the West Midlands Ambulance Service, posted vicious threats against Bailey on Facebook. He accused her of being solely responsible for the hospital’s negative reputation and wrote: 'I hope you suffer a life-threatening illness at night... because your local hospital is closed — your fault.' He added: 'Go back to yer bacon butties girl and leave the staff alone.' Shockingly, Guest’s own mother, Irene, died in 2008 at the same hospital after enduring neglect — she was left unwashed, unfed, and in soiled sheets. His father, Jeff, 82, is an active member of 'Cure the NHS'. Despite this personal connection, Guest targeted the very movement fighting for the dignity his mother was denied. Guest has since deleted the posts and issued an apology, according to the ambulance service, but remains under investigation. He has not been suspended. Bailey, 51, has contacted the police and expressed fear for her safety: 'If I need an ambulance urgently and he picks up the phone, can I trust this man?' She emphasized that while she has received overwhelming support from hardworking NHS staff, a minority of toxic individuals continue to harass her with threats of illness and death — a pattern that has persisted for five years. The Mid Staffordshire scandal sparked national outrage, prompting Prime Minister David Cameron to order inspections of 14 hospitals with high death rates. The trust remains under scrutiny by regulator Monitor and has already closed its overnight A&E unit due to staffing shortages.

article_content: Phillip and Nancy Garrido met while Phillip was serving time in federal prison for the 1976 kidnapping and rape of a 25-year-old woman from South Lake Tahoe, Nevada authorities revealed. The couple now faces 29 felony charges related to the 1991 abduction and 18-year captivity of 11-year-old Jaycee Lee Dugard in a hidden shed and tent compound in their Antioch, California backyard. Phillip Garrido’s criminal history began in 1977, when he was convicted of kidnapping and raping the woman after luring her into his car under false pretenses. Court records show he handcuffed her, bound her with a leather strap, and drove her to a storage unit in Reno, where he assaulted her. He told her the attack was 'her fault' because she was attractive. He served 11 years of a 50-year sentence at Leavenworth, Kansas. It was during this incarceration that he met Nancy Garrido, though details of their relationship remain undisclosed. Phillip’s father, Manuel Garrido, told CNN his son’s mental decline began after a motorcycle accident and LSD use in high school. 'He went crazy,' he said. 'He was an angel when he was young — it’s a damn shame.' Although Manuel hasn’t spoken to his son in 20 years and has never visited the Antioch home, he said he wasn’t surprised by the allegations. Phillip Garrido maintained a blog under the handle 'THEMANWHOSPOKEWITHHISMIND,' where he claimed divine visions, the ability to speak in 'the tongue of angels,' and control over sound through thought. His posts promoted 'God's Desire,' a church he ran from his home. One entry from August 2008 urged readers to 'witness what the world believes is impossible' and invited contact via email. In a separate 2007 post, he claimed his insights could help people who hear voices avoid violent acts. Since the case gained global attention, the blog has been flooded with angry, profane comments from outraged readers.

article_content: From an Italian prince and a Spanish gigolo to a Russian billionaire and a Vatican priest, Bambi Smyth has certainly dated her fair share of fascinating men. The 55-year-old Melbourne resident spent three months on 75 blind dates across 22 countries—all in pursuit of 'The One.' Her packed schedule took her to dinners with extraordinary individuals, each paired with a signature dish from their homeland. 'It was a cross between speed dating and a smorgasbord,' she told Daily Mail Australia. 'I wanted to meet as many men as possible—even if I only had one day in a country and was juggling two or three dates.' Of all her encounters, Stefano, an Italian naval architect, stood out. 'He was charm on steroids—generous, brilliant, and warm. Falling for him was an understatement,' she recalled. But like several others, Stefano was married. Smyth turned her search for love into a cultural experiment, documenting her experiences in her new book, Men on the Menu. Before leaving Australia, she emailed friends and acquaintances, requesting connections with single men aged 25–55 in exchange for helping her research a book on food and relationships. Not all dates were enchanting. In Hungary, a man calmly chopped chicken while remarking, 'If I had another career, I’d probably be a serial killer—I love chopping and I’m very neat.' She clutched her chair on the seventh floor of an unknown building. In Monaco, she suspected a man was a gigolo after he asked how many stars her hotel had. 'I didn’t fall for it,' she said. In Norway, a man fed her a pungent cheese called 'The Musician'—resulting in three straight days of flatulence that, she joked, let her play 'Oom Pah Pah' with her body. Not every encounter was memorable for the right reasons. In England, her cousin’s ex-boyfriend told her she was 'stupid' 37 times. In Brazil, her first international date stole extra cash from her wallet—then serenaded her. Yet, despite the odd, awkward, or painful moments, Smyth felt no regrets. After returning to Australia, she met Greg—and realized her journey had transformed her. 'I became less judgmental. I learned you can’t judge a book by its cover—or a man by his wallet.' Men on the Menu (The Five Mile Press, $32.95) is available from October 1, 2024, at bookstores and online at www.fivemile.com.au.

Hennes packade schema ledde henne till middagar med ovanliga män, varje en kopplad till en typisk rätt från deras hemland. 'Det var en blandning av speed-dating och en smörgåsbord,' sa hon till Daily Mail Australia. 'Jag ville träffa så många män som möjligt—även om jag bara hade en dag i ett land och mötte två eller tre män.' Av alla möten stod Stefano, en italiensk skeppsarkitekt, ut. 'Han var charm på steroider—generös, genial och varm. Att bli förälskad i honom är en underdrift,' minns hon. Men som flera andra var Stefano gift. Smyth vandrade sin kärlekssökning till ett kulturellt experiment och dokumenterade sina äventyr i sin nya bok, Män på Menyn. Innan hon lämnade Australien skickade hon e-post till vänner och bekanta och bad om kontakter med ensamma män mellan 25 och 55 år som skulle hjälpa henne med forskningen kring mat och relationer. Inte alla datum var förtrollande. 'Jag föll inte för det,' sa hon. I Norge gav en man henne en doftande ost kallad 'Musikern'—vilket resulterade i tre helt dagar med gas som, skämtade hon, gjorde att hon kunde spela 'Oom Pah Pah' med sin kropp. Inte alla möten var minnesvärda för rätt orsaker. I England berättade hennes kusins ex-käresta att hon var 'dum' 37 gånger. I Brasilien, hennes första internationella datum, stjal han extra pengar ur hennes plånbok—och sedan sjöng han för henne. Jag lärde mig att man inte kan döma en bok efter omslaget—eller en man efter hans plånbok.' Män på Menyn (The Five Mile Press, 32,95 AUD) är tillgänglig från den 1 oktober 2024 i bokhandlar och online på www.fivemile.com.au.
