article_content: Lord Tebbit today warned that disabled people could face pressure to 'do the right thing' and end their lives if the law is changed to permit assisted dying. In a moving speech, the former Conservative chairman revealed that his wife, Margaret — paralyzed in the 1984 IRA Brighton bombing — once told him, 'You'd be better off without me.' He said this illustrates how legalizing assisted dying might unintentionally pressure vulnerable individuals to choose death to spare their families hardship. Lord Tebbit emphasized that Margaret has endured constant pain for 30 years since the attack, and her suffering has intensified over time. His remarks came during a debate on Lord Falconer’s private member’s bill, which would allow doctors to prescribe a lethal dose to terminally ill patients with six months or less to live, provided they make a voluntary, clear, and informed request. The bill received an unopposed second reading in July after a 10-hour debate featuring nearly 130 speeches. Former Archbishop of Canterbury Lord Carey supported the bill despite previous opposition. Lord Tebbit argued that current laws act as a deterrent against wrongful pressure or assistance in suicide, and that the proposed changes would add procedures without strengthening protections. 'If someone wrongfully pressures another to end their life, they currently fear legal consequences,' he said. 'But under this bill, that deterrent disappears.' He drew a parallel to abortion law enforcement, citing cases where doctors unlawfully signed forms for sex-selective abortions without consequence. 'Where is the deterrence in that?' he asked. Over 170 amendments were tabled to the bill, and with limited parliamentary time, supporters fear delays could derail it. Disability rights advocates expressed alarm, while proponents accused opponents of trying to 'strangle' the legislation. Labour peer Lord Campbell-Savours shared that while he has lived with illness for 31 years, he hopes one day to have the legal right to end his suffering without court interference. Lord Winston stressed the need for robust safeguards, stating that medical professionals alone cannot be entrusted with such decisions. Justice Minister Lord Faulks confirmed the government would take a neutral stance and allow a free vote. Lord Falconer agreed that judicial oversight is essential, saying, 'In principle, I think... it will give greater protection.' Peers ultimately backed an amendment requiring a High Court judge of the Family Division to confirm that the patient’s wish to die is voluntary, clear, settled, and informed.

I en rörlig tal, avslöjade den före detta konservativa partiledaren att hans hustru, Margaret — paralyserad i IRA:s bombattack i Brighton 1984 — en gång sa till honom: 'Du skulle ha varit bättre utan mig.' Han sa att detta illustrerar hur att legalisera assistert död kan oavsiktligt trycka sårbara individer att välja död för att spara sina familjer från lidande. Lord Tebbit betonade att Margaret har lidit av konstant smärta i 30 år sedan attacken, och hennes lidande har intensifierats över tid. article_content: After intense negotiations that stretched into the early hours of Monday, world leaders in Durban, South Africa, reached a landmark climate deal aimed at slowing global warming. United Nations Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon called it a vital step forward, praising the agreement to extend the Kyoto Protocol — the international treaty requiring industrialized nations to reduce greenhouse gas emissions — beyond its 2012 expiration date. For the first time, countries agreed to begin drafting a legally binding climate agreement that would eventually include all major emitters, including China, India, and Brazil — a significant shift from past talks where developing nations were exempt. Alongside this, delegates launched the Green Climate Fund, pledging to mobilize $100 billion per year by 2020 to help poorer nations adapt to rising temperatures, extreme weather, and sea-level rise. U.S. climate envoy Todd Stern described the process as grueling but historic, noting that binding all top polluters under one legal umbrella marks a turning point. Britain’s climate minister, Chris Huhne, echoed this optimism, calling the outcome a 'credible package.' However, experts warned the deal stops short of immediate action. Elliot Diringer of the Center for Climate and Energy Solutions said the agreement barely held together until the final moments, calling its survival a win in itself. Meanwhile, humanitarian group Oxfam sharply criticized the results, pointing out that the fund has no guaranteed money behind it and that major emitters like the U.S. and Canada are not bound by the extended Kyoto Protocol. Oxfam warned that without stronger measures, African farmers could see crop losses exceeding 50% within a generation, and global food prices could surge by more than double — nearly half of that increase driven by climate disruption.

För första gången enades länderna om att börja utarbeta ett juridiskt bindande klimatavtal som till slut ska gälla alla stora utsläppsländer, inklusive Kina, Indien och Brasilien — en betydande förändring från tidigare förhandlingar där utvecklingsländer var undantagna. Samtidigt lanserade delegationerna Gröna klimatfonden, med löftet om att samla in 100 miljarder dollar per år till 2020 för att hjälpa fattigare länder att anpassa sig till stigande temperaturer, extrema väderförhållanden och havsnivåökning. article_content: Millennials are moving in large numbers to coastal cities—but not necessarily the largest ones. According to a SmartAsset analysis of 268 U.S. cities based on the 2022 U.S. Census Bureau’s 1-Year American Community Survey, Cambridge, Massachusetts, saw the highest percentage of millennial movers relative to its population in 2022. It was followed by Santa Clara, California, and Seattle. SmartAsset defines millennials as individuals aged 25 to 44. Jaclyn DeJohn, SmartAsset’s managing editor for economic analysis, told Business Insider that the common driver behind these relocations is opportunity. 'The diversity within the top 10 cities reflects people choosing different lifestyles and paths,' she said. In Cambridge, many millennials relocated for graduate programs at Harvard and MIT, employment opportunities in nearby Boston, and the city’s high quality of life. Nearly 17,300 millennials moved to Cambridge in 2022, making up nearly 15% of all newcomers—and raising the city’s total millennial population share to 38%. Santa Clara, a tech hub in Silicon Valley home to Intel and NVIDIA, attracted over 16,600 millennials last year—about 13.3% of its population—pushing the millennial share to 40%. Despite a median home sale price exceeding $1.5 million, according to Redfin, the area remains a magnet for tech talent. Austin’s growing tech sector and Georgia’s emerging film industry have drawn millennials to Sandy Springs, DeJohn noted. In 2022, one in four millennials moved to a new city. While many relocated for work, others in remote roles sought lower costs of living or a slower pace. 'Millennials are older now than they’ve ever been,' DeJohn added. 'People are starting to settle down and have families. A lot of the traditional life script at that point is to move out to the suburbs for more space—so that’s likely happening in large numbers.' Seattle and Sunnyvale, California, also saw strong inflows, with millennials making up roughly 12.5% of their populations. Both cities attracted well-paid tech workers able to absorb high housing costs. Other top destinations included Denver, Bellevue, Washington, and Arlington, Virginia—where 5.2% of the total population were millennial migrants from out of state. Hialeah, Florida, and Arlington were especially popular among foreign-born millennials. Meanwhile, Killeen, Texas—home to Fort Hood military base—ranked eighth overall. When ranked by total millennial population share—not just new arrivals—Jersey City, New Jersey, led at 41.5%, followed by Seattle, Denver, and Austin. At the other end, Port St. Lucie, Florida, had the lowest millennial mover rate at 4.8%, followed by Brockton, Massachusetts. Several California cities—including Fontana, Santa Ana, and Moreno Valley—had rates under 6%. For Gen Xers, the top relocation destinations in 2022 were Surprise, Arizona; Bend, Oregon; Scottsdale, Arizona; and Orlando, Florida—with Florida claiming three of the top ten spots.

Jaclyn DeJohn, chefredaktör för ekonomisk analys vid SmartAsset, sa till Business Insider att den gemensamma drivkraften bakom dessa flyttningar är möjligheter. 'Den diversitet vi ser i de tio första städerna speglar bara att människor väljer olika livsstilar och vägar,' sa hon. I Cambridge flyttade många millennials för gradprogram vid Harvard University och Massachusetts Institute of Technology, arbetsmöjligheter i närliggande Boston och stadens höga levnadsstandard. Santa Clara, en techhub i Silicon Valley med huvudkontor för Intel och NVIDIA, har lockat mycket talang under de senaste åren, trots en mycket hög bostadsprisnivå—medelpriset för en bostad är över 1,5 miljon dollar, enligt Redfin. 'En stor del av det traditionella livsskriptet vid den punkten är att flytta ut till förorterna och få lite mer plats för familjen. Så det är troligt att mycket av detta händer där.' Seattle och Sunnyvale i Kalifornien såg också jämförbara flyttningar, eftersom millennials som flyttade år 2022 utgjorde cirka 12,5 % av totalbefolkningen i båda städerna. Båda såg ett inflöde av techarbetare som kunde förmå sig att betala de höga prissättingarna. Städer som Denver, Bellevue i Washington och Arlington i Virginia såg också stora inflöden av millennials. Arlington hade den högsta andelen millennialmigranter från andra delstater: 5,2 % av totalbefolkningen. Hialeah i Florida och Arlington var särskilt populära städer för utländska millennials. Killeen i Texas, belägen ungefär mitt emellan Austin och Waco, rankades åttonde på listan som hemvist för militärbasen Fort Hood. När man tittar på de bästa städerna efter andel totala millennials i förhållande till totalbefolkningen, låg Jersey City i New Jersey först med 41,5 %, följt av Seattle, Denver och Austin. Men Port St. Lucie i Florida hade den lägsta andelen millennials som flyttade in i förhållande till totalbefolkningen: 4,8 %, följt av Brockton i Massachusetts. Städer i Kalifornien som Fontana, Santa Ana och Moreno Valley hade alla under 6 %. SmartAsset undersökte också vart Gen X flyttade förra året. De bästa städerna var Surprise i Arizona; Bend i Oregon; Scottsdale i Arizona; och Orlando. Florida utgjorde tre av de tio bästa städerna.

article_content: Chelsea are furious after the Football Association refused to punish Burnley’s Ashley Barnes for a dangerous tackle on Nemanja Matic during their 1-1 draw. Referee Martin Atkinson, who has since been removed from this weekend’s officiating schedule, confirmed he saw both the tackle and Barnes’s later kick at Branislav Ivanovic — meaning the FA applied its rule that retrospective sanctions only apply to incidents missed by match officials. Matic, however, was sent off for retaliating and received a three-match ban, which Chelsea are now appealing as disproportionate. Manager Jose Mourinho labeled the challenge 'criminal' on Sky Sports, going so far as to question whether Barnes even qualifies as a footballer. Burnley manager Sean Dyche countered, asserting that slow-motion replays distorted the incident and that Barnes clearly won the ball. Additional controversy arose when reports surfaced that Chelsea captain John Terry showed teammates visible stud marks on his legs from Barnes’s challenge and pointed out a bruise near his eye, allegedly caused by an elbow during the game. The FA emphasized that its retrospective system targets unseen fouls — like stamping or kicking — not those observed live. To strengthen their case, Chelsea plan to submit expert opinions from former players Gary Neville and Alan Shearer, who’ve supported similar reactions in the past. Atkinson, who issued only three yellow cards in one of the season’s most physical matches, has been reassigned as fourth official for Manchester United’s upcoming fixture against Sunderland. Mourinho, previously fined £25,000 for alleging a campaign against his club, will not be penalized for his latest comments. The FA’s three-member independent panel is meeting today to rule on Matic’s appeal — a decision that could reshape how player retaliation is judged in future cases.

article_content: The South African government has announced plans to deploy armed troops to its wildlife parks to protect rhinoceroses from poachers targeting their valuable horns. The initiative — which may include helicopter gunships patrolling park skies and soldiers equipped with night-vision goggles on the ground — comes as new data reveals that more rhinos have been killed in South Africa this year than at any time since the colonial era. So far in 2012, 588 rhinos have been killed by poachers linked to Far Eastern criminal networks that sell rhino horn for use in traditional medicine. A carcass of a 24-year-old rhino cow at Finfoot Lake Reserve was among eight killed in a single incident this month — underscoring the scale of the crisis. Most rhino horns end up in China or Vietnam, where they are falsely believed to cure ailments such as cancer and impotence. This year’s toll of 588 rhinos far exceeds the 448 killed in 2011 and is nearly 4,500% higher than the 13 rhinos killed in 2007. With approximately 22,000 rhinos — 80% of the world’s population — South Africa is home to the majority of remaining white and black rhinos. Experts warn that poaching has reached a critical threshold: more rhinos are dying than being born. Earlier this month, a poaching gang killed eight rhinos in Kruger National Park, including a calf. The animals were shot, then their horns — valued at £60,000 per kilogram on the black market — were forcibly removed. Some were further mutilated; one female had her genitalia severed. Jason Bell, Director of the International Fund for Animal Welfare, condemned the brutality: 'The numbers of rhinos being poached continue to rise sharply. In 2012 alone, deaths have nearly doubled compared to two years ago, with most occurring in Kruger National Park — arguably one of the most secure habitats for wildlife.' In response, North West Premier Thandi Modise declared: 'The cruelty and brutality inflicted upon rhinos — symbols of our ecological heritage — have gone too far. Recent events demand extraordinary measures to safeguard our biodiversity and tourism.' While details remain unclear, previous proposals included armed military patrols at night and aerial surveillance. Poaching syndicates often operate with similar sophistication, using helicopters and night-vision gear to target rhinos at close range or tranquilize them before killing them with machetes. Rhino horn is composed of keratin — the same protein found in human fingernails — and there is no scientific evidence supporting its medicinal properties. Although unverified, some suggest that rhino populations during the colonial era fell as low as 3,000 individuals, potentially making today’s losses comparable in magnitude.

article_content: Just three months after lifting the World Cup trophy in Brazil, Germany’s national team is in turmoil. After three Euro 2016 qualifying matches, they have managed only one win and one draw — the worst start ever by a German or West German side in a major tournament qualifier. Even their narrow victory over Scotland felt hollow. Defeats to Poland and a shocking 1-1 draw with the Republic of Ireland on Tuesday have left the team reeling. The German media have not held back: Tagesspiegel sarcastically suggested Gibraltar — Germany’s next opponent — might be planning a win. Bild demanded answers: 'How bad is the atmosphere among our World Cup winners?' The mood on the pitch told its own story. After John O’Shea’s 94th-minute equalizer, the German players trudged off in silence — no handshakes, no conversation. The unity that defined their World Cup triumph was gone. No excuses were made. Jerome Boateng admitted: 'We can only blame ourselves. Losing the ball so carelessly late in the game invites disaster.' Manuel Neuer, visibly shaken, said: 'It’s incredibly irritating. We had the three points in our hands.' Despite controlling possession against both Poland and Ireland, Germany failed to convert chances. With stars like Thomas Müller, Toni Kroos, Mario Götze, and André Schürrle available — even amid injuries to Schweinsteiger, Khedira, and Özil — the expectation was clear: they should have won. The root causes are multifaceted. Mental and physical exhaustion from the grueling World Cup campaign has drained creativity and focus. Players assumed dominance would automatically lead to goals — it didn’t. The squad is also in transition. Newcomers like Sebastian Rudy, Karim Bellarabi, and Antonio Rüdiger show promise but haven’t yet integrated into the tightly knit unit that won in Brazil. Even some World Cup veterans — Matthias Ginter, Erik Durm, Julian Draxler — lack consistent international experience. Perhaps the biggest void is the absence of captain Philipp Lahm. As Pep Guardiola once noted, Lahm possessed unmatched on-field intelligence and concentration. His leadership wasn’t just vocal — it was tactical. His replacement, Schweinsteiger, is also injured, leaving a leadership vacuum. Nine World Cup winners took the field against Ireland — yet questions remain: Where are the leaders? The German public isn’t angry yet — just bewildered. Fans, typically quick to boo underperformers, stayed quiet. Too stunned to react. Löw still retains public trust. His World Cup triumph earned him leeway. But if results don’t improve, the knives will come out again.

article_content: As Norway grapples with its deadliest violence in decades, attention centers on Anders Behring Breivik, the 32-year-old man charged with the Oslo bombing and the mass shooting at a Labour Party youth camp on Utoya Island. Although police had not officially named him at the time, Norwegian media widely identified him as Breivik. A 1,518-page manifesto, allegedly authored by Breivik, laid out a radical ideology opposing multiculturalism, Muslim immigration, and what he termed 'cultural Marxism.' It also served as a blueprint for violent revolution, titled '2083: A European Declaration of Independence.' Photos show Breivik with blond hair, blue-green eyes, and chiseled features—sometimes dressed in preppy attire, other times in military-style gear. His lawyer, Geir Lippestad, confirmed that Breivik planned to explain his actions in court. According to Norway’s official weapons registry, Breivik legally owned a Glock pistol, a rifle, and a shotgun. He was also registered as running a business producing vegetables, melons, and tubers—a venture that gave him access to large quantities of ammonium nitrate fertilizer, commonly used in explosives. An employee at Felleskjøpet Agr confirmed Breivik purchased six tons of fertilizer in May 2011. She initially saw nothing unusual, given his farm, but alerted police after the attacks. Breivik was exempt from Norway’s mandatory military service and had no formal military training. He was a member of the conservative Progress Party until 2007, which advocates reducing immigration. A senior party member compared meeting Breivik to 'meeting Hitler before World War II.' In his manifesto, Breivik praised the Progress Party as the only major political force opposing 'the madness of Muslim immigration,' but claimed deeper loyalty to a fictional pan-European militant network called the 'Conservative Revolutionary Movements in Europe,' identifying himself as a 'Justiciar Knight.' The manifesto condemned multiculturalism, blamed Norway’s government for enabling the 'Islamification of Europe,' and cited grievances including NATO’s intervention in Kosovo, Norway’s apology over the Muhammad cartoons, and the Nobel Peace Prize awarded to Yasser Arafat. Breivik referenced online forums like Document.no, where he expressed fear of Islamic youth harassment and criticized left-wing groups such as Blitz, SOS Rasisme, and Rød Ungdom, accusing them of intimidating conservatives. He outlined a three-phase plan for a future European civil war: open-source warfare (through 2030), formation of clandestine cells (2030–2070), and a final coup to install a hardline conservative regime by 2083—with the ultimate goal of expelling Muslims from Europe. Although he claimed sole responsibility, police did not rule out potential accomplices, as his manifesto referenced a broader network of sympathizers. Breivik anticipated being labeled a monster but believed history would remember him as a martyr defending European culture and Christendom.

article_content: Scientists believe Mars had an oxygen-rich atmosphere more than a billion years before Earth did. Analysis of meteorites and surface rocks suggests oxygen was influencing the Martian surface around 4 billion years ago—long before oxygen accumulated significantly in Earth’s atmosphere, which occurred roughly 2.5 billion years ago. Using data from NASA’s Spirit rover, which explored ancient terrain on Mars containing rocks over 3,700 million years old, researchers found evidence that these rocks had been exposed to oxygen before being recycled into the planet’s interior and later ejected via volcanic activity. Martian meteorites found on Earth originated from deeper within Mars, where oxygen exposure was minimal. Comparisons between these meteorites and surface rocks reveal compositional differences best explained by an early abundance of oxygen on Mars. This finding, published in the journal Nature, raises questions about the origins of oxygen on Mars: Was it produced biologically, as on Earth during the Great Oxygenation Event (GOE), or through abiotic chemical reactions? Lead scientist Professor Bernard Wood from Oxford University stated: 'Mars likely had an oxygen-rich atmosphere about 4 billion years ago—well before Earth’s GOE around 2.5 billion years ago. Since oxidation gives Mars its red color, the planet was probably wet, warm, and rusty long before Earth’s atmosphere became oxygen-rich.' In May, NASA’s Curiosity rover discovered rounded pebbles indicating sustained water flow nearly 2 billion years ago. Pebbles form only when transported over long distances by liquid water, making this compelling evidence of ancient rivers. Separately, NASA’s Opportunity rover detected evidence of neutral, potentially drinkable water in June 2013—marking the first time water on Mars was found in a non-acidic form. Previously, all liquid water signatures were linked to sulfuric acid. These discoveries strengthen the case that Mars once possessed conditions suitable for life. While no direct evidence of life exists yet, the presence of both oxygen and drinkable water expands the possibilities for past biological activity.

article_content: WASHINGTON (CNN) — American U-2 reconnaissance aircraft have been conducting surveillance flights along the Turkey-Iraq border to monitor military activity, according to three U.S. military sources. This comes ahead of high-level talks between U.S. and Turkish officials and a regional conference aimed at reducing tensions between Turkey and Kurdish PKK rebels operating across the border. Turkey, a key NATO ally and host of the U.S.-operated Incirlik Air Base, has been urging Washington to provide greater support in combating PKK cross-border attacks. Pentagon spokesman Geoff Morrell confirmed Wednesday that the U.S. is significantly increasing its intelligence-sharing with Turkey. 'We are assisting by supplying them, the Turks, with intelligence — lots of intelligence,' Morrell said. Ankara has warned it may launch a full-scale military operation into northern Iraq if Iraqi and Kurdish authorities fail to neutralize the PKK. U.S. and Iraqi diplomats are working to dissuade Turkey from such a move. Recent clashes near the border saw Turkish forces targeting suspected rebel positions, with fighting spilling into northern Iraq. On Thursday, U.S. Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice will meet with Turkish officials in Ankara, while President George W. Bush holds talks in Washington with Turkish Prime Minister Recep Tayyip Erdogan. A regional summit involving Iraq and other neighboring nations is also scheduled for Thursday and Friday in Istanbul. Iranian Foreign Minister Manouchehr Mottaki has joined mediation efforts, meeting with Iraqi leaders in Baghdad and offering 'full support' for the Istanbul conference. His participation prompted a delay in his planned visit to Lebanon, according to Iran’s state media. Meanwhile, tensions between Washington and Ankara have been exacerbated by proposed U.S. congressional legislation that would formally recognize the World War I-era killings of Armenians as genocide. Turkey responded by recalling its ambassador and threatening to restrict U.S. access to Incirlik Air Base. In response, sponsors of the bill have requested a delay in the vote.

article_content: Robin van Persie has openly admitted his form this season has been below expectations, and he remains uncertain whether Manchester United will offer him a new contract when his deal expires in 18 months. Once the prolific scorer who led United to the 2012–13 Premier League title with 26 goals, the Dutch striker has managed just eight strikes so far this campaign. His relationship with manager Louis van Gaal was strained early on, especially after a disappointing performance against Arsenal in November. Though his play has improved since, Van Persie was left frustrated after missing a key chance in Friday’s 0–0 FA Cup draw against lower-league side Cambridge United. Speaking at the launch of Swissquote — United’s new global forex and trading partner — alongside teammates Angel di Maria, Juan Mata, and David de Gea, Van Persie took full responsibility for his scoring drought. 'I’ve played around 20 games and scored eight,' he said. 'I’m not happy. I know what I need to do. I’ve done it for 10 years — I’ll keep doing it.' He emphasized that football is often decided by tiny margins: 'One chance. Two chances. You have to take them.' He referenced missed opportunities against Tottenham and Cambridge, noting how easily outcomes could have changed with a single conversion. Van Persie, who turns 32 in August 2015, acknowledged that his future is out of his hands. 'I’m here for the next 18 months. After that? I don’t know. It’s not up to me.' Despite tactical growing pains under Van Gaal — particularly the shift to a three-man defense — Van Persie remains confident in the process. 'We believe in him. We’re creating chances. We’re winning games. It’s a process.' He also noted the team’s morale lifted after Manchester City and Chelsea were eliminated from the FA Cup, leaving United as the last remaining top-flight club in the competition. 'We’re the highest-ranked team left. That’s something to be proud of.' Meanwhile, Real Madrid’s potential signing of David de Gea appears increasingly unlikely, as FIFA has opened an investigation into their recruitment of two underage players from Venezuela in 2012. If found guilty, Madrid could face a transfer ban — a penalty that would block any summer moves, including de Gea’s. Real maintains they followed regulations, claiming the players never officially played for the club and were withdrawn once concerns arose. Their case hinges on whether the boys' families relocated for non-football reasons — a condition required under FIFA rules for non-EU signings under 18.

En gång den produktiva målskytt som ledde United till Premier League-titeln 2012–13 med 26 mål, har den nederländske stöten klarat bara åtta mål hittills denna säsong. Hans relation med tränare Louis van Gaal blev spänd tidigt, särskilt efter en besvikande prestation mot Arsenal i november. Trots att hans spel har förbättrats sedan dess, blev Van Persie frustrerad efter att ha missat en nyckelchans i fredagens 0–0-draw i FA-cupen mot lag från lägre ligan Cambridge United. Vid lanseringen av Swissquote — Uniteds nya globala forex- och handelspartner — tillsammans med lagkamrater Angel di Maria, Juan Mata och David de Gea, tog Van Persie fullt ansvar för sin målsnålhet. 'Jag har spelat runt 20 matcher och gjort åtta mål,' sa han. 'Jag är inte nöjd. Jag vet vad jag behöver göra. Jag har gjort det i 10 år — jag kommer att fortsätta.' Han noterade också att lagets humör förbättrades efter att Manchester City och Chelsea blev utslagna från FA-cupen, vilket lämnade United som det enda överlevande topplagslaget i tävlingen. 'Vi är det högst rankade laget kvar. Det är något att vara stolta över.' Real hävdar att de följde reglerna, och att spelarna aldrig officiellt spelade för klubben och drogs tillbaka när bekymmer uppstod. Deras fall bygger på om barnens familjer flyttade för icke-fotbollsorsaker — ett krav enligt FIFA-regler för icke-EU-spelare under 18 år.

article_content: CNN — With national polls and those in key battleground states nearly tied just days before November 6, the winner of the presidential election remains anyone’s guess. So, by the numbers, here are some unusual predictors of past presidential elections: 62.1% — Sales share of the President Obama Chia planter as of October 23. 37.1% — Sales share of the Mitt Romney Chia planter as of October 23. 80% (4 out of 5) — The percentage of Family Circle magazine’s Presidential Cookie Bake-off winners who later became First Lady after their husbands won the presidency. (Cindy McCain was the sole exception.) 54% — The proportion of recipes in the Family Circle bake-offs that include chocolate chips. 16 — The number of consecutive presidential elections, from 1936 to 1996, in which the incumbent party retained office if the Washington Redskins won their final home game before Election Day. (The so-called 'Redskins Rule' did not hold in 2000, 2004, or 2008.) 60% — Sales share of the Barack Obama mask at Spirit Halloween stores. 40% — Sales share of the Mitt Romney mask at Spirit Halloween stores. 8 out of 9 — The number of correct predictions made by General Cinema movie theaters’ 'StrawVote' polls between 1968 and 2000. In 2000, moviegoers incorrectly predicted Al Gore would win. 16 — States, primarily in the upper Midwest and the South, where the '7-Election' coffee cup poll by 7-Eleven cannot be conducted due to the absence of 7-Eleven stores. 59% — The share of votes Barack Obama received in the 7-Eleven poll as of October 31. 51% — The percentage of students who voted for Barack Obama in the Scholastic Student Vote. 45% — The percentage of students who voted for Mitt Romney in the Scholastic Student Vote. 10 — The number of times since 1908 a National League baseball team has won the World Series in an election year. 67% — Based on historical trends, the likelihood a Democrat would win the presidency when a National League team won the World Series. 33% — Based on historical trends, the likelihood a Republican would win the presidency under the same condition. 4 — The number of games played in the 2012 World Series. The National League’s San Francisco Giants swept the American League’s Detroit Tigers. 1 — In 2012, Punxsutawney Phil did not see his shadow — one of only a few times this occurred during an election year. (Romney sought to make Pennsylvania competitive.) 1 — Punxsutawney Phil saw his shadow on Groundhog Day in 2012. 9 — The number of nuts eaten from Mitt Romney’s bowl by Gnocchi, the election-predicting squirrel from South Carolina, compared to five from Obama’s bowl. Gnocchi correctly predicted Obama’s victory in 2008.

article_content: In a soft voice, teenager Austin Sigg confessed in gruesome detail how he abducted a 10-year-old girl from his Colorado neighborhood and dismembered her. But what Sigg could not explain to police detectives was why. 'It was a random place, a random time — random everything,' Sigg told officers in an interrogation video released this week. 'I was just driving, kind of looking around. I saw her... found a place to park, pulled over, waited, and when she walked by, I grabbed her.' Sigg, who was 17 at the time, kidnapped Jessica Ridgeway on October 6, 2012. He told police he got her into his car, bound her hands and legs, and drove around for 20 minutes as she screamed and pleaded with him. 'I would lie to her,' he said. 'I told her everything would be okay. I just lied.' He took the bespectacled, blonde girl to his home. Details of what happened there were partially redacted from the released footage. Sigg also confessed to an earlier attempted kidnapping of a jogger earlier that year. Sigg was turned in by his mother, who called 911 and handed the phone to him. Jessica was missing for five days before authorities arrested him. Last week, Sigg was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole for murder, plus 98 additional years for other charges. The judge stated he expected Sigg to remain incarcerated for the rest of his natural life. During the trial, members of Jessica’s family wore purple — her favorite color. 'This monster took away the light of my life,' said Christine Ridgeway, Jessica’s grandmother. 'It shattered the core of my family.'

article_content: Simone Battle, a 25-year-old singer and former 'X Factor' contestant, tragically died by suicide in West Hollywood on Friday, according to the Los Angeles County Coroner’s Office. Once on the brink of mainstream success, Battle was a member of G.R.L., the girl group launched in 2012 as a successor to the Pussycat Dolls. This year, the group gained traction with their single 'Wild Wild Love,' featuring rapper Pitbull, which climbed to No. 30 on the Billboard Hot 100. Their most recent release, 'Ugly Heart,' dropped in June. Battle’s boyfriend discovered her unresponsive in a closet around 7:45 a.m. Friday after last seeing her alive at 3:45 a.m. An autopsy confirmed suicide as the cause of death. Pitbull expressed grief on social media, writing, 'My heart and prayers go out to @GRLSimone and her family.' G.R.L.’s official Twitter account honored her memory, stating, 'Simone's incredible talent was only surpassed by the size of her heart.' Raised in Los Angeles, Battle began performing in church choirs as a child, trained in ballet and tap, modeled in commercials, and interned with a company linked to the Black Eyed Peas. She studied music and songwriting at the University of Southern California before auditioning for 'The X Factor,' where she made it to the top 16. Her most notable acting role was in Mario Van Peebles’ 2012 film 'We the Party.' In interviews, she credited Whitney Houston as the inspiration behind her musical dreams.

article_content: The U.S. Supreme Court has turned down an urgent request from Odyssey Marine Exploration, a Florida-based salvage firm, to keep control of nearly half a billion dollars’ worth of gold and silver coins while legal disputes over ownership continue. The coins were recovered from the wreck of the Spanish warship Nuestra Señora de las Mercedes, which sank in 1804 after being attacked by British ships near what is now Portugal. Spain has consistently prevailed in U.S. courts—from the federal district court in Tampa to the appellate court in Atlanta—and now, the highest court has declined to step in. Justice Clarence Thomas, responsible for emergency matters from Florida, rejected the motion without explanation. Jim Goold, Spain’s lead attorney, called the outcome a definitive win, noting the Supreme Court rarely accepts fewer than 1% of similar appeals. Odyssey’s legal team expressed disappointment but acknowledged the improbability of reversal. The company still has one pending request before the justices, though experts doubt it will succeed. According to Spanish officials, the majority of the roughly 600,000 coins—many of them historic ‘pieces of eight’ minted in Lima, Peru—are currently stored in Florida. Spain’s Culture Minister, Jose Ignacio Wert, emphasized that the treasure is not being reclaimed for profit but as a vital piece of national heritage. He confirmed plans to exhibit the coins in Spanish museums and hinted at possible collaborations with institutions in Latin America, including Peru, whose territory was the original source of many of the artifacts. Although Peru has not filed a formal claim, Wert said Spain remains open to sharing parts of the collection to honor its broader regional history.

Mynten återfunnits från vraket av det spanska krigsfartyget Nuestra Señora de las Mercedes, som sjönk år 1804 efter ett angrepp av brittiska skepp nära det som nu är Portugal. article_content: The Czech Republic has apologized for a controversial art installation it commissioned to mark its six-month presidency of the European Union. The work, titled 'Entropa,' is a large-scale multimedia model depicting satirical stereotypes of EU member states. Created by Czech artist David Cerny, it features Bulgaria represented as a Turkish-style toilet and Romania as a vampire-themed amusement park — imagery that sparked widespread outrage. Betina Joteva, spokesperson for Bulgaria’s permanent representation to the EU, called the work 'preposterous and a disgrace,' stating it 'humiliated the Bulgarian nation and offended our national dignity.' At the official unveiling in Brussels, Czech Deputy Prime Minister Alexandr Vondra acknowledged the offense, saying: 'Entropa is a provocation. I understand that some may feel offended, and I apologize — not only to Bulgaria, but to any member state harmed by this.' He added, 'If this work was meant to mock anyone, it was first and foremost us.' Other nations were also caricatured: Germany appeared crisscrossed by autobahns resembling a swastika; Spain as an endless construction site; Luxembourg as a golden nugget labeled 'For Sale'; the Netherlands as a flooded land with minarets rising above the water; and Poland reimagining the iconic Iwo Jima flag-raising with Catholic clergy waving a rainbow pride flag. The United Kingdom was notably absent, possibly reflecting its complex relationship with the EU. In a further embarrassment, the Czech government revealed it had been misled. Its original brief called for a collaborative project involving 27 artists — one from each member state. However, the final installation bore the names of 26 fictitious artists, all fabricated by Cerny and his collaborators, Kristof Kintera and Tomas Pospiszyl. Vondra stated: 'We created the conditions for a joint project. We were unpleasantly surprised to discover that the participation of 27 artists was misinformation.' Although the government initially feared taxpayer money had been misused, Cerny later confirmed that all costs were privately funded. Cerny and his team apologized to Czech Prime Minister Mirek Topolanek and other ministers, admitting they had 'failed to inform them of the truth and misled them.' According to Cerny’s website, the plan to involve 27 artists collapsed due to time and budget constraints, leading to the creation of fictional personas — some with their own websites — to maintain the illusion. David Cerny is no stranger to controversy. In 1991, he was arrested for painting a Soviet tank in Prague pink. His portfolio includes provocative pieces such as 'Jesus Christ' and 'Dead Raped Woman,' as well as a bronze fountain depicting two men urinating toward each other.
translated_content: Tjeckien har beklagat sig för en kontroversiell konstinstallation som det kommissionerade under sitt sex månader långa ordförandeskap i Europeiska unionen. Verket, som heter 'Entropa,' är en stor multimedia-modell som avbildar satiriska stereotyper av EU-medlemsländerna. Skapat av den tjeckiske konstnären David Cerny, visar det Bulgarien som en turkisk toalett och Rumänien som ett vampyrtemapark — bilder som utlöst bred oro. Betina Joteva, talesperson för Bulgariens permanenta representation vid EU, kallade verket 'absurdt och en skam,' och sa att det 'förnedrade den bulgariska nationen och kränkte vår nationella värdighet.' Vid den officiella avslöjandet i Bryssel sa den tjeckiske vice premiärministern Alexandr Vondra: 'Entropa är en provokation. Jag förstår att vissa kan känna sig kränkta, och jag vill be om ursäkt — inte bara för Bulgarien, utan för alla medlemsländer som blivit skadade av detta.' Han tillade: 'Om detta verk var tänkt att skämta med någon, så var det först och främst oss själva.' Andra länder blev också karikatyrer: Tyskland syntes kors och tvärs med motorvägar som påminde om en hakenkors; Spanien som en oavslutad byggarbetsplats; Luxemburg som en guldglansande nötklump med etiketten 'Att sälja'; Nederländerna som ett översvämmande land där minareter stiger ovanför vattnet; och Polen som återskapar det ikoniska flagghävandet på Iwo Jima, men med katolska präster som viftar med en regnbågflagga. Storbritannien saknades tydligt, möjligen som spegling av dess komplexa förhållande till kontinenten. I en ytterligare besvikelse avslöjade tjeckiska regeringen att den hade blivit lurad. Ursprungligt uppdrag var ett samarbetsprojekt med 27 konstnärer — en från varje medlemsstat. Men den slutliga installationen bar namnen på 26 fiktiva konstnärer, alla skapade av Cerny och hans samarbetare, Kristof Kintera och Tomas Pospiszyl. Vondra sa: 'Vi skapade förutsättningarna för ett gemensamt projekt. Vi var obehagligt förvånade över att upptäcka att deltagandet av 27 konstnärer var en missinformation.' Även om regeringen ursprungligen fruktade att skattebetalarnas pengar hade använts, bekräftade Cerny senare att alla kostnader täcktes av privata medel. article_content: Britain could be forced to contribute to its own EU rebate under unacceptable new Brussels plans, which would cost the UK more than £800 million over seven years. European Council President Herman van Rompuy unveiled the proposal as part of his latest outline for the next seven-year EU budget. Initially, van Rompuy suggested the UK might retain its £3.2 billion-a-year rebate — famously secured by Margaret Thatcher in 1984. However, detailed proposals reveal that the UK would be expected to fund a portion of its own rebate moving forward. Officials did not specify the exact amount, but if paid at the UK’s standard 13% EU contribution rate, it would cost £416 million per year — nearly £3 billion over seven years. New documents indicate van Rompuy may push for a 25% reduction in the rebate between 2014 and 2020, totaling £5.6 billion in lost savings. British government sources insisted the rebate — already reduced by Tony Blair — is 'non-negotiable'. A senior official also rejected a compromise proposal that would increase EU funding above inflation. Prime Minister David Cameron has signaled he will veto any budget exceeding a real-terms freeze when negotiations begin later this month. 'Our position is extremely clear,' a source said. 'The Prime Minister has said he wants a budget freeze at worst — and with his veto last year, he has shown he is serious.' MPs voted earlier this month to cut the EU budget. In 1984, Thatcher secured the rebate by demanding 'our own money back' during a summit in Fontainebleau, France, threatening to withhold Britain’s payments until EU leaders relented. Tory MP Mark Reckless called van Rompuy’s plan 'ludicrous': 'A rebate we have to pay for ourselves is not a rebate — it is a complete non-starter and suggests they are not serious about reaching a deal.' He added: 'There has been a parting of the ways between the EU leadership and the British people — and the gap is now so wide it is hard to see how a deal can be done.' Van Rompuy’s proposal represents a modest reduction from Brussels’ original demand of €1 trillion (£800 billion). But a real-terms freeze would require cutting the proposed budget by up to £160 billion — far beyond what van Rompuy is willing to accept. British sources believe a freeze is possible but unlikely. 'The landing pad is the size of a postage stamp — and it’s covered in trip wires,' one source said. Officials fear the summit may end in deadlock, with a final decision delayed until next year — or even canceled to allow van Rompuy to save face.

article_content: Duran Duran are suing their official fan club, Worldwide Fan Clubs Inc., for $40,000 (£23,500) over allegations that the club failed to pay agreed-upon fees and maintain proper accounting records. The band, best known for their 1980s hits 'Hungry Like The Wolf' and 'Girls on Film,' filed the lawsuit in Cook County Circuit Court against the Glenview, Illinois-based organization. According to court documents, Worldwide Fan Clubs Inc. entered into a contract with Duran Duran in 2010 to establish and operate an official fan club. The agreement stipulated that the club would sell merchandise and collect membership fees, remitting 75% of profits to the band. The contract also required the club to maintain accurate financial and membership records — claims the band’s legal team say were not fulfilled. Duran Duran released their debut single, 'Planet Earth,' in 1981, which reached No. 12 on the UK charts. Later that year, 'Girls on Film' peaked at No. 5. In 1983, 'Is There Something I Should Know' became their first UK No. 1, also reaching No. 4 in the US. Their 1984 single 'The Reflex' topped the UK charts again. Their most recent studio album, 'All You Need Is Now,' released on March 21, 2011, received critical acclaim but underperformed commercially compared to earlier releases. In a blog post on their official website, the band confirmed they are working on a new album featuring guitar work by John Frusciante of Red Hot Chili Peppers.

The victim sustained swelling in her finger, shoulder, and hip, along with substantial pain, per a police report. He is scheduled to return to court later this year to face charges of assault, forcible touching, sexual abuse, and harassment. Since directing his last film, Night Of The Zombies, in 1981, Reed has largely stepped away from filmmaking. article_content: A time capsule hidden for more than a century at one of Boston’s most popular tourist attractions was opened on Friday. According to the Bostonian Society, which maintains the 1713-built Old State House, the rectangular copper box — containing artifacts from 1901 — was sealed inside one of the two iconic statues atop the building: a lion and a unicorn. These statues have stood there for centuries. The Bostonian Society did not fully disclose the capsule’s contents, explaining that 'the process of extracting documents that are old and likely fragile requires slow and careful handling.' However, a February 24, 1901, article in the Boston Globe detailed what was placed inside. The article predicted the capsule would 'prove interesting when opened many years hence.' Among the items were photographs and autographs of local leaders, including Massachusetts Governor Winthrop M. Crane and Boston Mayor Thomas Norton Hart; news clippings from several city newspapers; and a letter to posterity written by reporters assigned to City Hall. Also included was a photograph of the 5th Massachusetts Regiment en route to Framingham to be mustered in as U.S. volunteers for the Spanish-American War, along with campaign buttons for William McKinley, Theodore Roosevelt, and John D. Long, who ran for vice president. The capsule was sealed within the lion’s head by Samuel Rogers, a local coppersmith who worked on the renovation of the nearly 200-year-old State House. Despite the event being covered by Boston’s largest newspaper at the time, the Bostonian Society’s current staff had no knowledge of the capsule until they received a letter from a descendant of Rogers revealing its location.

article_content: In a major address at the United Nations in New York, President Barack Obama expressed openness to direct talks with Iran’s President Hassan Rouhani—even though Iranian officials declined a planned meeting. Obama stressed that while the U.S. recognizes decades of hostility—including hostage-taking and attacks on American personnel—it believes resolving Iran’s nuclear ambitions could pave the way for a new relationship grounded in mutual respect. He affirmed that the U.S. supports Iran’s right to peaceful nuclear energy, but is firmly committed to stopping any move toward nuclear weapons. To that end, Obama said he’d personally written to both Rouhani and Supreme Leader Khamenei, urging diplomacy over confrontation. On Syria, Obama demanded a binding UN Security Council resolution to verify that the Assad regime follows through on its promise to dismantle its chemical weapons stockpile. He called the August 21 attack in Ghouta—killing more than 1,400 civilians—an undeniable crime by the Syrian government, dismissing claims that rebels were responsible as 'an insult to human reason.' He praised UN inspectors for risking their lives under sniper fire to gather irrefutable evidence, calling them heroes of global accountability. While rejecting regime change as U.S. policy in Syria, Obama acknowledged the devastating cost of civilian suffering and pledged an additional $339 million in humanitarian aid, bringing total U.S. support to nearly $1.4 billion. He emphasized that who leads Syria must be decided by Syrians alone, warning that past U.S.-led interventions elsewhere had unintended, often disastrous consequences. Still, he argued that U.S. engagement remains vital for national security. Defending the idea of American exceptionalism, Obama countered critics like Russian President Vladimir Putin, who warned against self-perceived superiority. 'America stands up for the interests of all,' he said. Meanwhile, some U.S. lawmakers, including Rep. Ed Royce, urged harsher sanctions on Iran, comparing Obama’s diplomacy to what they called the failed approach with North Korea in the mid-2000s. Former UN Ambassador John Bolton dismissed the UN as merely a forum for competing national agendas—not a true institution.

article_content: The anguished family of Corporal Geoffrey McNeill, a soldier killed by his comrade in a violent attack at their barracks following a late-night drinking session, have labeled his murderer 'dishonourable and cowardly' after he was sentenced to life in prison. Afghan veteran Corporal Geoffrey McNeill, 32, was murdered by 23-year-old Lance Corporal Richard Farrell at Clive Barracks in Tern Hill, Shropshire, in March. Farrell consistently denied involvement in the killing but was found guilty by a jury after a four-week trial at Birmingham Crown Court. After Farrell received a life sentence, the victim’s family stated that the punishment was 'not comparable' to the 'immeasurable, unforgettable, and indefinite' devastation caused by McNeill’s brutal murder. In a statement, they said: 'While we are pleased that justice through the courts has prevailed, there remains a void in our lives that will never be filled. The sentence received by Richard Farrell is not comparable to the sentence carried by those who knew and loved Geoff, for which there is no limit. The actions of Richard Farrell have significantly impacted Geoff’s family and friends, including his colleagues within the Army. The devastation caused is immeasurable, unforgettable, and indefinite.' The family, who attended the entire trial, described McNeill as a man of 'ambition, drive, and potential,' whose life—and future opportunities, including starting a family—were stolen from him. 'We would like Geoff to be remembered for the legend he was, and not for the dishonourable, cowardly, and brutal way in which he was taken from us,' they added. McNeill was found dead in his room in March. Farrell raised the alarm after discovering his body. The pair had been out drinking in Market Drayton the previous night, during which McNeill punched Farrell in a pub altercation, injuring both men. Court testimony revealed that Farrell had an unaccounted period of three and a half hours early that morning. McNeill’s neck was broken in three places; he was also punched in the head, stomach, and genitals. Sentencing, Judge Melbourne Inman QC told Farrell he had carried out a 'very severe assault' but clarified: 'That is not how you killed Mr McNeill. You killed him by sustained pressure to his neck, either with a ligature or manually, like some form of arm hold.' The judge noted that McNeill had dug his fingernails into his own neck in a desperate attempt to break the hold, leaving visible marks. He concluded there was clear premeditation and that Farrell abandoned the body after the killing. Despite Farrell’s claim of total memory loss due to consuming at least a litre of Disaronno liqueur, the jury accepted the prosecution’s argument that he inflicted a series of heavy blows and deliberately strangled McNeill. There was no prior history of hostility between the two men, who served in different companies. Surveillance footage showed McNeill flooring Farrell in a pub, cutting his own knuckle and Farrell’s lip. Farrell later admitted to having provoked McNeill with verbal taunts. After returning to barracks around 3 a.m., Farrell’s whereabouts were unverified until 6:30 a.m., when he was found asleep in the guard room. A soldier reported hearing 'bumping noises' and someone saying, 'Geoff — calm down,' between 4 a.m. and 4:30 a.m. Farrell reportedly woke up, showered, washed his clothes, and asked another soldier, 'Where’s McNasty’s room?'—referring to McNeill—claiming he couldn’t remember anything and wanted to apologize. When he entered McNeill’s room at approximately 9:15 a.m., Farrell claimed to have found him lying on the floor in only his underwear and attempted resuscitation. However, prosecutors noted that such efforts would have transferred DNA, which was not found. Farrell also told police he squeezed McNeill’s testicles 'to check for consciousness,' citing Army training. Judge Inman described McNeill as 'a hugely well-liked and respected soldier' and 'a loved and trusted comrade,' adding that the family’s statements were deeply moving and that healing would take a very long time.

I ett uttalande sa de: 'Vi är nöjda med att rättvisan genom domstolarna har segrat, men det finns en tomhet i våra liv som aldrig kommer att fyllas. Det straff som Richard Farrell fått är inte jämförbart med det straff som de som kände och älskade Geoff bär, eftersom det inte har någon gräns. Farrells handlingar har påverkat Geoff:s familj och vänner, inklusive hans kollegor inom armén. Den förstörelse som orsakats är obmätbar, oupphörlig och obegränsad.' Familjen, som satt i hela rättegången, beskrev McNeill som en man med 'ambition, drivkraft och potential,' vars liv — och framtida möjligheter, inklusive att bli förälder — blev stulna. 'Vi vill att Geoff ska minnas som den legenden han var, och inte för det oförärliga, modlösa och våldsamma sätt på vilket han togs ifrån oss alla,' tillade de. McNeill hittades död i sitt rum i mars. Farrell larmade efter att ha upptäckt hans kropp. Paret hade varit ute och druckit i Market Drayton kvällen innan, då McNeill slog Farrell i en pub, vilket skadade båda. Domstolen fick veta att Farrell hade en obeskriven tid på tre och en halv timme tidigt på morgonen. McNeills hals var brutet på tre ställen; han blev också slagen i huvudet, magen och könsdelarna. Under domfallet sa domaren Melbourne Inman QC till Farrell att han utfört ett 'mycket allvarligt övergrepp', men förtydligade: 'Det är dock inte hur du dödade Mr McNeill. Du dödade honom genom hållande tryck på hans hals, antingen med en snara eller manuellt, som en typ av armbågegrepp.' Domaren noterade att McNeill hade skrapat sina naglar så hårt mot sin egen hals i ett desperat försök att bryta greppet, vilket lämnade synliga märken. Han kom fram till att det fanns tydlig förberedelse och att Farrell lämnade kroppen efter mordet. Trots Farrells påstående om total minnesförlust på grund av att ha druckit minst en liter Disaronno-likör godkände juryen åklagarens argument att han utövat en serie tunga slag och medvetet strangulerat McNeill. Det fanns inget tidigare fiendskap mellan de två männen, som tjänstgjorde i olika kompanier. Övervakningsfilmer visade att McNeill drog ner Farrell i en pub, där han skadade sin egen knoge och Farrells läpp. Farrell erkände senare att han provokert McNeill med ord. Efter att ha återvänt till kasernen runt 3 a.m. var Farrells plats okänd till 6:30 a.m., när han hittades sovande på golvet i vaktlokalen. En soldat rapporterade att han hörde 'slagsmålsljud' och någon som sa 'Geoff – lugna dig' mellan 4 och 4:30 a.m. Farrell uppstod, duschar, tvättade sina kläder och frågade en annan soldat: 'Var är McNasty:s rum?' — i syfte att hitta McNeill — och hävdade att han inte kunde minnas något och ville be om ursäkt. När han gick in i McNeills rum cirka 9:15 a.m. påstod Farrell att han hittade honom liggande på golvet i bara underkläder och försökte hjälpa honom. Men åklagaren noterade att sådana försök skulle ha lämnat DNA-spår, vilket inte hittades. Farrell berättade också för polisen att han tryckte på McNeills testiklar 'för att se om han var medveten,' enligt sin militära utbildning. Domaren Inman beskrev McNeill som 'en mycket välbehaglig och respekterad soldat' och 'en älskad och förtrodd kamrat,' och tillade att familjens uttalanden var mycket rörande och att det skulle ta mycket lång tid för dem att förstå döden och dess omständigheter.

article_content: A 10-year-old boy’s message in a bottle — filled with thoughts about football and video games — has traveled more than 2,500 miles across the Atlantic Ocean and washed ashore in the Azores. Curtis Kipple, a fourth-grader at Fred W. Hill School in Brockport, New York, wrote the letter alongside his classmates in December 2010. The bottles were released into the Gulf Stream by a fisherman from North Carolina’s Outer Banks. Last week, Curtis’s bottle was discovered in the small fishing village of Terceira, part of the Azores archipelago off Portugal. The news left him and his teacher, Chris Albrecht, overwhelmed with emotion. 'It was really special,' Albrecht told the Democrat and Chronicle. 'About 80% of my students have never seen the ocean. That Curtis’s bottle made it across the Atlantic is pretty amazing.' Curtis, now in fifth grade, said he wrote about playing football with his dad and enjoying video games. 'I was blown away,' he added. The glass bottles were set adrift 30 miles offshore in December 2010. Curtis’s was found by a father and son while fishing near Terceira. Ana Ponte, 25, a local resident, emailed the school to share the discovery: 'My brother and father went out to sea to catch seafood common here — and we found a bottle with a message from a boy named Curtis Kipple.' This isn’t the only success story: Another student, Adam VerSteeg, had his bottle found in June 2011 on the beach of Clam Harbour, Nova Scotia, Canada, by Jude Major. 'The project exceeded my wildest expectations,' Albrecht said. 'Finding both bottles is mind-blowing.'

'Cirka 80 procent av mina elever har aldrig sett havet. Att Curtiss flaskan hann över Atlanten är ganska fantastiskt.' Curtis, som nu går i femte klass, sa att han skrev om att spela fotboll med sin pappa och njuta av datorspel. 'Jag var chockad,' la han till. article_content: As Congress heads into its August break, lawmakers are scrambling to wrap up several pressing issues — though many will likely wait until September. At the top of the list: the border funding showdown. With agencies facing a cash crunch next month, Republicans and Democrats remain far apart. The Senate Democrats propose $2.7 billion, House Republicans are pushing for under $1 billion, and President Obama asked for $3.7 billion. The real hurdle? Whether to amend a 2008 law designed to protect child migrants from Central America. GOP lawmakers want to tie new funding to faster deportations, arguing the current process drags on for years. Democrats resist, fearing it would undermine protections for kids escaping gang violence. Even within the administration, signals are mixed — top officials hint at openness, while Hispanic leaders draw firm red lines. Meanwhile, veterans’ health care has seen rare bipartisan progress. After CNN exposed deadly delays and secret waiting lists at VA hospitals, public outrage forced action. Senator Bernie Sanders and Representative Jeff Miller unveiled a $17 billion agreement to fix systemic failures, hire more staff, and reduce backlogs. The Senate is expected to confirm Robert McDonald — former Procter & Gamble CEO and West Point graduate — as the new VA secretary as early as Tuesday. Over 100 House members even urged Congress to stay in session until a bill passes. The Highway Trust Fund, which relies on gas taxes to pay for road repairs, is nearly empty. Fuel-efficient cars, lower driving rates, and stagnant gas tax rates have drained its reserves. Congress is considering a temporary $11 billion bailout from general funds — a short-term fix that kicks the can to May. Without federal support, states could halt or cancel infrastructure projects, costing jobs and slowing economic activity. In another flashpoint, the House plans to vote on authorizing Speaker John Boehner to sue President Obama over his decision to delay the Affordable Care Act’s employer mandate. Republicans argue this was an abuse of executive power, despite having previously supported similar delays themselves. Democrats call the lawsuit a political stunt aimed at energizing the base ahead of midterms. Meanwhile, calls to impeach Obama remain fringe — polls show most Americans oppose it. Finally, with the fiscal year ending September 30, Congress has yet to pass full-year funding bills. The House has approved roughly half; the Senate hasn’t voted on any. To avoid another shutdown, Boehner expects a continuing resolution to extend current funding into December. Lawmakers will have just 10 days after Labor Day to strike a deal.

Demokraterna i Senaten föreslår 2,7 miljarder dollar, republikanerna i Representanthuset driver för mindre än 1 miljard, och president Obama bad om 3,7 miljarder. Det verkliga hinderet? Om man ska ändra en lag från 2008 som är avsedd att skydda barnmigranter från Centraltamerika. Republikaner vill koppla ny finansiering till snabbare utvisningar, eftersom den nuvarande processen tar år. Demokrater motstånd, rädd för att det skulle undergräva skydd för barn som flyr gängvåld. Även inom administrationen är signalerna blandade – höga experter antyder öppenhet, medan latinsamerikanska ledare sätter tydliga gränser. Samtidigt har veteranernas hälso- och sjukvård sett sällsynt bipartisk framsteg. Efter att CNN avslöjade dödliga förseningar och hemliga väntelistor vid VA-sjukhus tvingade offentlig upprördhet till handling. Senator Bernie Sanders och representant Jeff Miller lanserade ett 17 miljarder dollar stort avtal för att åtgärda systemiska brister, anställa mer personal och minska bakloggar. Senaten förväntas bekräfta Robert McDonald – tidigare vd för Procter & Gamble och West Point-graduate – som ny VA-sekreterare redan på tisdag. Mer än 100 representanter uppmanade dessutom Kongressen att hålla sig i session tills en lag antas. Vägtrafikfonden, som finansieras genom bensinbeskattning för att betala för väg- och broreparationer, är nästan tom. Bensinbesparingar, minskad körning och oförändrade bensintaxor har tömt den. Kongressen överväger ett tillfälligt 11 miljarder dollar stöd från allmänna skattemedel – en kortfristig lösning som skjuter upp problemet till maj. Utan federalt stöd kan delstater stoppa eller avbryta infrastrukturprojekt, vilket kostar arbetsplatser och saktar ner ekonomisk tillväxt. I en annan konflikt planerar Representanthuset att rösta om att ge talman John Boehner rätt att klaga på president Obama för hans beslut att fördröja arbetsgivarnas hälsoförsäkringsplikt enligt Affordable Care Act. Republikaner hävdar att detta var ett missbruk av exekutiv makt, trots att de själva tidigare stött liknande fördröjningar. Demokrater kallar målet för en politisk manöver för att mobilisera väljare inför mittvalen. Samtidigt är anhängare av att avsätta Obama en minoritet – en undersökning visar att de flesta amerikaner är emot det. Slutligen, med det ekonomiska året som slutar den 30 september, har Kongressen inte godkänt fulla budgetlagar. Representanthuset har godkänt cirka hälften; Senaten har inte röstat om någon. För att undvika en ny stängning förväntas Boehner införa en övergångsresolution som förlänger nuvarande finansiering till december. Lagstiftarna har bara tio dagar efter Labor Day för att komma till en överenskommelse.

article_content: On Saturday, the Congress party dropped Mahesh Joshi, a senior minister in Ashok Gehlot’s cabinet, and selected R.R. Tiwari, District Congress President (Jaipur City), as its candidate for the Hawa Mahal Assembly constituency. Tiwari’s name appeared in the sixth list of 23 candidates released by the party late Saturday. With this announcement, the total number of candidates declared so far stands at 179, with 21 more still to be announced. Joshi’s removal signals that the party’s high command has overridden Chief Minister Gehlot, who previously held considerable influence over candidate selections. While the Congress has largely retained its sitting MLAs, this decision marks a clear shift in power dynamics. In September last year, Joshi was one of three Gehlot-aligned leaders who led a boycott of the Congress Legislative Party (CLP) meeting, reportedly convened to empower the high command to select a new chief minister—widely believed to be Sachin Pilot. Joshi had been a key strategist in Gehlot’s camp, playing a critical role during the 2020 political crisis by coordinating MLAs and acting as Chief Whip to counter internal and external threats. However, the rebellion triggered anger among the high command, and Joshi became one of three targets for sidelining. The party has yet to announce a candidate for Kota North, the constituency of cabinet minister Shanti Dhariwal. Dharmendra Rathore, another key figure in the 2020 rebellion and not an MLA, also sought a ticket but remains unfielded. The timing of Joshi’s deselection coincides with personal setbacks: the Enforcement Directorate conducted raids on officials in his Public Health Engineering Department over allegations of corruption. The move is widely interpreted as an effort to placate Sachin Pilot’s faction, which has consistently criticized the CLP boycott. It also reinforces the high command’s declining authority in Rajasthan over recent years. Abhimanyu Poonia, a former NSUI state president and student leader aligned with Pilot, has been fielded from Sangaria. Other younger candidates have also been chosen: Shahjad Khan (son of 2018 losing candidate Ayub Khan and now an RPSC member) in Soorsagar, and Manish Yadav in Shahpura. Among those dropped were MLA J.P. Chandelia, replaced by Peetram Kala in Pilani. In Chomu, the party selected Dr. Shikha Meel Barala over 2018 losing candidate Bhagwan Sahai Saini and Rukshmani Kumari, president of the Rajasthan chapter of the All India Professionals’ Congress. Lokesh Sharma, CM’s Officer on Special Duty, had sought a ticket from Bhilwara but was passed over in favor of Om Narayaniwal. In Malpura, Ghasi Lal Choudhary was chosen over former state party president Dr. Chandrabhan. Although the Congress had left the Bharatpur seat to RLD in 2018—a move that resulted in a BJP win—it has once again opted to cede the seat to RLD. The incumbent minister, Subhash Garg, is expected to contest from Bharatpur under RLD’s banner.

I Chomu har partiet valt Dr. Shikha Meel Barala istället för 2018-förloraren Bhagwan Sahai Saini eller Rukshmani Kumari, ordförande för Rajasthan-avdelningen av All India Professionals’ Congress. Även om Kongresspartiet lämnade valetkretsen Bharatpur till RLD 2018 — ett beslut som resulterade i en BJP-vinst — har det återigen valt att överlämna platsen till RLD. article_content: In 1972, Terry Dietrich had her first car — a Corvette Stingray — stolen from the parking lot of her workplace in Duluth, Georgia. Six months after purchasing it, police believed the vehicle had been stripped for parts and dumped in the Chattahoochee River. But 42 years later, authorities contacted her: the car had been found. The catch? Dietrich no longer legally owns it. After the theft, her insurer, Allstate, paid out the claim and took legal title to the vehicle. Since then, neither Allstate nor the state of Georgia can issue her a new title. The car’s rediscovery came thanks to Gary Green, a car restorer who purchased it from a widow in North Carolina. While inspecting the vehicle, he noticed inconsistencies in the VIN. A second, hidden VIN revealed it matched the 1972 stolen Corvette — not the 1969 model listed on the paperwork. He immediately alerted police, who confirmed the theft report from November 1972. The car, remarkably well-preserved, remains impounded. Dietrich, who still lives in the same home she did in 1972, hopes to reclaim it. But without a court order — which she cannot afford — the vehicle will eventually be sold at a police auction. 'If I could get that car back, it could roll back up the same driveway, pull back into the same carport it left on 11-14-72. How awesome is that?' Dietrich told 11 Alive. Yet, if she can’t have it, she says she doesn’t want to see it at all. 'I’ll have to get over losing it all over again.'

Problemmet? Dietrich äger inte längre den lagligt. Efter stölden betalade hennes försäkringsbolag, Allstate, ut skadeståndet och tog över äganderätten till bilen. Sedan dess kan varken Allstate eller delstaten Georgia utfärda ett nytt registreringsbevis till henne. Bilens återupptäckt kom tack vare Gary Green, en bilspecialist som köpte den från en änka i North Carolina. När han undersökte bilen upptäckte han oenigheter i VIN-numret. Ett dolt, andra VIN-nummer visade att det var en stulen Corvette från 1972 — inte den 1969-modell som stod i dokumenten. Han meddelade genast polisen, som bekräftade stöldrapporten från november 1972. Bilen, som är förvånansvärt välbevarad, hålls fortfarande inkasserad. Dietrich, som fortfarande bor i samma hem som 1972, hoppas få tillbaka den. Men utan en domstolsorder — som hon inte kan betala för — kommer bilen att säljas på en polisauktion. 'Om jag kan få tillbaka min bil, kan den köra tillbaka upp samma drivväg, köra in i samma bilskörd den lämnade den 11-14-72. Hur fantastiskt är det inte?' sa Dietrich till 11 Alive. Men om hon inte kan ha den, säger hon att hon inte vill se den alls. 'Jag måste lära mig att förlora den igen.'

article_content: Cherie Blair, a distinguished UK barrister and one of the first 76 women to earn the prestigious title of Queen’s Counsel in 1995, has spent decades fighting for gender justice — both in courtrooms and across continents. In 2008, she launched the Cherie Blair Foundation for Women, dedicated to helping female entrepreneurs in Africa, South Asia, and the Middle East gain economic independence. In a candid conversation with CNN, she reflected on her journey from a modest upbringing, shaped by her mother’s resilience after being abandoned by her father and forced to raise two daughters alone. Her mother, who left school at 14 to become an actress, instilled in her the belief that education and self-reliance were non-negotiable. Today, Blair balances her demanding legal career with her foundation work by leveraging her flexible schedule as a self-employed barrister. She frequently travels for both cases and foundation projects — recently returning from Nigeria, where she combined legal outreach with grassroots initiatives. While she admits juggling both roles is rarely neat or perfectly timed, she credits her foundation’s dedicated team of 17 professionals for keeping daily operations running smoothly. Her passion centers on empowering women financially, believing that when women control their own income, they gain the power to choose their futures — whether it’s pursuing education, refusing early marriage, or escaping exploitation. Even in countries like the UK, she stresses, human trafficking and gender-based coercion persist. As Chancellor of the Asian University for Women in Bangladesh, she continues to invest in systemic change through education, always guided by one goal: a world where no woman is treated as less than equal.

Hon startade Cherie Blair Foundation for Women år 2008, en organisation som stöder kvinnliga entreprenörer i Afrika, Sydasien och Mellanöstern att uppnå ekonomisk självständighet. I ett ärligt samtal med CNN reflekterade hon över sin väg från ett beskedligt uppväxte, formad av moderns mod efter att ha blivit försummad av fadern och tvingad att uppfostra två döttrar ensam. Hennes mor, som lämnade skolan vid 14 års ålder för att bli skådespelerska, överförde till henne att utbildning och självförtroende var icke-förhandlingsbara. Idag balanserar Blair sin krävande juridiska karriär med sitt stiftelsesarbete genom att utnyttja sin flexibla arbetsmodell som självständig advokat. Hon reser ofta för både fall och stiftelsesprojekt — nyligen återkom från Nigeria, där hon kombinerade juridisk utbildning med lokala initiativ. Trots att hon erkänner att balansen mellan båda roller sällan är perfekt eller ordentlig, tackar hon stiftelsens dedikerade team på 17 professionella för att hålla dagliga operationer igång. Hennes passion ligger i att stärka kvinnor ekonomiskt, och hon tror att när kvinnor har kontroll över sina egna inkomster, får de makt att välja sina framtider — om de vill fortsätta utbilda sig, undvika tidig äktenskap eller fly undan utnyttjande. Även i länder som Storbritannien, betonar hon, förekommer människohandel och könsbaserad tvång. Som kansler vid Asian University for Women i Bangladesh investerar hon fortfarande i systemförändring genom utbildning, alltid guidad av ett mål: en värld där ingen kvinna behandlas som mindre värd.

article_content: Canadian Member of Parliament Chandra Arya shared a purported video on social media platform X, alleging that Khalistani supporters in Surrey, British Columbia, plan to target the Hindu Laxmi Narayan Mandir. He urged Canadian authorities to intervene, stating, 'Last week, Khalistani supporters verbally abused a Sikh family outside a Sikh Gurdwara in Surrey, BC, according to some reports. Now it appears the same group wants to create trouble at the Hindu Laxmi Narayan Mandir.' Arya emphasized that Hindu temples in Canada have repeatedly been targeted in recent years, calling such acts hate crimes against Hindu-Canadians. 'Allowing these things to continue openly and publicly is not acceptable,' he said. In August 2023, a Hindu temple in Canada was vandalized with Khalistan referendum posters featuring Hardeep Singh Nijjar — a figure designated as a terrorist by India and killed in Surrey on June 18, 2023. This was not an isolated incident: in April, the BAPS Swaminarayan Temple in Windsor was defaced with anti-India graffiti; in February, the Ram Mandir in Mississauga suffered similar damage; and in January, the Gauri Shankar Mandir in Brampton was vandalized. The Consulate General of India in Toronto condemned each incident and called for investigations and accountability. Tensions between India and Canada escalated after Prime Minister Justin Trudeau claimed in Parliament that Canadian security agencies had reason to believe 'agents of the Indian government' were involved in Nijjar’s killing. India dismissed the allegation as 'absurd' and 'motivated,' and has not provided public evidence to substantiate the claim. Notably, while India designates Nijjar as a terrorist, Canada has not, and he was legally recognized as a resident and community leader in British Columbia. In September, India suspended visa services to Canada. However, in October, it resumed four categories — entry, business, medical, and conference visas — following a review of recent Canadian measures aimed at improving security cooperation.

article_content: By Sam Greenhill. PUBLISHED: 20:09 EST, 23 December 2012. | UPDATED: 08:54 EST, 24 December 2012. Stress: Former Chief Whip Andrew Mitchell has spoken of the torment he endured as the 'Plebgate' scandal unfolded. Andrew Mitchell says he stopped eating, lost over a stone in weight, and struggled to get out of bed as the 'Plebgate' storm raged. In his first detailed account of the scandal, he described sitting for hours with his BlackBerry, consumed by fears for his career. In an article published yesterday, the former chief whip detailed how the crisis affected him and his family. Mitchell, 56, and his wife Sharon, a GP, have two daughters: Rosie, 21, and Hannah, 25. 'By day four, I couldn't sleep. I stopped eating. The weight fell off me—I lost more than a stone in the first three weeks,' he said. 'Sharon lost almost as much. Day after day, the press assault continued.' 'On several days, I simply couldn't get out of bed. I'd sit for hours with my BlackBerry in one hand and my old mobile in the other.' 'Nighttime was the worst. We’d sleep for two hours, then wake and toss and turn for the rest of the night as I feared the destruction of my career.' 'At 3 a.m., facing the wall after another day of relentless attacks, aware of more damaging stories looming, I wondered if I could keep going.' The initial strategy was to ride out the storm. The MP for Sutton Coldfield retreated to his Nottinghamshire home, where his family was preparing for Rosie’s 21st birthday. 'None of us had any idea what was about to happen.' He claims the media painted him as a 'monster,' prompting nearly 1,000 hostile emails in the first weekend alone—and taking a heavy emotional toll. Mitchell, who also owns a home in London, said reporters interviewed his neighbors—most of whom described his family as 'nice'—but one revealed decades of pent-up resentment. 'Twenty-four years of bitterness erupted publicly,' he said. CCTV footage from Downing Street showed Mitchell cycling toward the side gate after being denied exit through the main gates. Mitchell was brushing his teeth when Prime Minister David Cameron called and urged him to resign after learning of a 'toxic' email allegedly from a member of the public that seemed to support the police version of events. 'It was completely untrue,' Mitchell insisted. After a tense six-minute conversation, he convinced Cameron to give him another chance. But his attempt to move past the controversy with a public apology backfired—and he resigned on October 19.
